author: puhtahtoe
body:
As discussed in #14 and [this](https://github.com/koreader/koreader/issues/13629#issuecomment-2816647908) KOReader issue, it looks like the current problem with syncing on KOReader 2025.4 is due to how the rest client library KOReader uses reads the ```content-type``` header. 

It appears that the root cause of the problem is that Spore is looking for exactly ```application/json``` in the ``content-type``` header. When sending a response using the StatusCode method in C#, ```charset=utf-8``` is automatically appended to the ```content-type``` header. This causes Spore to mistakenly fail to recognize the response body as JSON.

By manually serializing the JSON and sending the response as a basic ContentResult we can explicitly set the ```content-type``` without C# "helping" us.

- Lighting toggled to baked only for realtime lights around elevator and in living hub generally/bathrooms

- Turned ladder back on in smugglers roon
- Removed animator on airlocks for hangar
- Swapped elevator interactables and adjusted their height

- Fixed colliders to be round and fit better on Table, Side Table, Coffee, and Storage models
- Fixed cracks and light leak in both door models
- Made all platform materials a bit lighter so that they should absorb lighting less
- Adjusted Creature Material and its VFX material also
- Tweaked Hanging fern Collider 
 
# World Aligned Material
- Blur between planes now working leading to much smoother transitions, overall node system has less nodes which should make it run better also
- Metal control for base and noise added
- Smoothness control for base and noise added
- Applied to walls and columns, still refining the look of this but will likely use in a few other spots.
- Applied to white furniture items as test, this will be tweaked more before final build

This pull request introduces several changes to improve the deployment process, update asset handling, enhance test coverage, and fix minor issues in the Angular application. The key changes include adding a GitHub Actions workflow for deploying to GitHub Pages, updating `angular.json` and `package.json` for static asset handling and deployment, replacing the `NewsApiService` with a new implementation, and enhancing test coverage for components and services.

### Deployment Improvements:
* [`.github/workflows/publish-ghpages.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-136d975becf69a4ecb756ecd2e72782ee43b021f74cbd00efef8eeb070422c2eR1-R27): Added a GitHub Actions workflow to automate deployment to GitHub Pages for the `main` and `feature/*` branches. The workflow installs dependencies, builds the project, and runs the `deploy-ghpages` script using a GitHub token.
* [`package.json`](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L10-R10): Added a `deploy-ghpages` script to deploy the application using `ng deploy` with a base href. Installed the `angular-cli-ghpages` package to enable deployment. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L10-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R37)

### Asset Handling Updates:
* [`angular.json`](diffhunk://#diff-2d2675bb4687601a5c7ccf707455132f90f3516a33716185687e5c41df59ac7dL27-R31): Simplified the `assets` configuration to include `src/favicon.ico` and `src/assets` while removing custom glob patterns for images. Added a deploy configuration using `angular-cli-ghpages`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2d2675bb4687601a5c7ccf707455132f90f3516a33716185687e5c41df59ac7dL27-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2d2675bb4687601a5c7ccf707455132f90f3516a33716185687e5c41df59ac7dL102-R98)

### Test Coverage Enhancements:
* [`src/app/core/services/news-api.service.spec.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-870666e418b3b222b54cd91965530fb94a847740ce47dce9175174583180e933R1-R166): Added comprehensive unit tests for `NewsApiService` to verify API calls, parameter handling, and error propagation.

Changes:
- Ran [buildifier](https://github.com/bazelbuild/buildtools/blob/v8.0.3/buildifier/README.md) to apply auto-fixes in the `BUILD.bazel` file.
- Updated Bazel version to `8.2.1`
- Added a `.bazelrc` file which activates incompatibility flags checked by BCR CI
- Updated `MODULE.bazel` by converting dev dependencies to normal dependencies so analysis can pass for external consumers.

body:
This pull request introduces significant changes to the application, including the addition of role-based authentication, CRUD operations for chapters, and updates to the project's structure and documentation. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Role-Based Authentication and Middleware
* Added `LoginController` and `RegisterController` to handle login and registration for `student` and `lecturer` roles, including validation and redirection logic. (`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.php` - [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dd8f74be860904029d6fedf114e59c3a428add429a01bf7276e3f9b5a768d594R1-R55) `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.php` - [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6bf28759467ab9d7b7bdf08ccb156d3c4096c034096f086eca89a0cb1d2316c8R1-R64)
* Introduced a `CheckRole` middleware to enforce role-based access control. (`app/Http/Middleware/CheckRole.php` - [app/Http/Middleware/CheckRole.phpR1-R17](diffhunk://#diff-a1c097ddb8c48745a21bd420aeaa8d5e755e9cd485117d3b987ab82ca4cb85d9R1-R17))
* Registered the `role` middleware in `Kernel.php`. (`app/Http/Kernel.php` - [app/Http/Kernel.phpR66](diffhunk://#diff-df6b23c7ec651a76ba2081a6e22960428ffab37044fe22a2e523355c54a12399R66))

### Chapter Management
* Added `ChapterController` to handle CRUD operations for chapters, including file uploads, validation, and authorization. (`app/Http/Controllers/ChapterController.php` - [app/Http/Controllers/ChapterController.phpR1-R127](diffhunk://#diff-27655a91cf12a1d0b05ff21b228c4a112b276597107ba9c6470bbc74f0c176c8R1-R127))
* Created a `Chapter` model with a list of subjects and necessary attributes for chapter management. (`app/Models/Chapter.php` - [app/Models/Chapter.phpR1-R36](diffhunk://#diff-e31e4075d474319024a7861cb50695fa6b0db78f6916f194a61f7ee8d059c454R1-R36))
* Defined a `ChapterPolicy` to manage authorization for chapter-related actions. (`app/Policies/ChapterPolicy.php` - [app/Policies/ChapterPolicy.phpR1-R95](diffhunk://#diff-9d650d334b52a5f5d505bd98fb75441b89f69e0b3ab9afeebb6c1a12ee3bcc53R1-R95))
* Registered the `ChapterPolicy` in `AuthServiceProvider`. (`app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php` - [app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.phpR5-R6](diffhunk://#diff-9d0a077acda375ef8f06f27e2f823037207bcbaa21c2c87cf4c113a13a3eb0c4R5-R6))

### User and Profile Management
* Updated `UserController` to include methods for managing lecturer and student dashboards, as well as profile viewing and editing. (`app/Http/Controllers/UserController.php` - [app/Http/Controllers/UserController.phpR5-R83](diffhunk://#diff-8e91484f56a38d906339650a2e3af6dbda84b6a43e6d889b792bd55b53a54e76R5-R83))
* Added `Lecturer` and `Student` models extending `Authenticatable` for role-based user management. (`app/Models/Lecturer.php` - [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c916ee2021758ab0a36c1e39eab0b7d5520c80aa6ece711f893e296c0626d35R1-R28) `app/Models/Student.php` - [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e0efb0a9b01e1f6f417e509746ce690b099f5fc1a2e093510095c0d0414a9a4fR1-R28)
* Updated the `User` model to include a `role` attribute. (`app/Models/User.php` - [app/Models/User.phpR24](diffhunk://#diff-37a2d7d879a7de3f7d73b2975cd22be9f41ec10c334a0dda9ad1e869332e4ecbR24))

### Cleanup and Deprecation
* Removed unused models, including `Event` and `Subject`, which are no longer relevant to the updated structure. (`app/Models/Event.php` - [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-45c2422d278ff0f70b1a349fd17abcf1c924d9090d7fccc78d473e3941a6205dL1-L15) `app/Models/Subject.php` - [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c3e1dbcc0d62ae4a1e0c80a61fee09da6eb030788357c2a8d1fca5ff6d6a1d62L1-L23)

author: akirakyle
body:
The following microbenchmarks show that using `Base.PermutedDimsArray` over `_permutedims` gives an over 50x speedup for sparse arrays while still retaining the same performance for dense arrays. This means that the two separate implementations of `permutesystems` can be unified into one function.

```julia
using BenchmarkTools
using SparseArrays

function _permutedims(x::AbstractSparseMatrix, shape, perm)
    shape = (shape...,)
    shape_perm = ([shape[i] for i in perm]...,)
    y = spzeros(eltype(x), x.m, x.n)
    for I in eachindex(x)::CartesianIndices # Help with inference (detected by JET)
        linear_index = LinearIndices((x.m, x.n))[I.I...]
        cartesian_index = CartesianIndices(shape)[linear_index]
        cartesian_index_perm = [cartesian_index[i] for i=perm]
        linear_index_perm = LinearIndices(shape_perm)[cartesian_index_perm...]
        J = Tuple(CartesianIndices((x.m, x.n))[linear_index_perm])
        y[J...] = x[I.I...]
    end
    y
end

function permute1(A,N)
    A = Base.ReshapedArray(A, (N,N,N,N), ())
    A = PermutedDimsArray(A, (1,3,2,4))
    A = Base.ReshapedArray(A, (N^2, N^2), ())
    copy(A)
end

permute2(A,N) = _permutedims(A, (N,N,N,N), (1,3,2,4))

function permute3(A,N)
    A = reshape(A, (N,N,N,N))
    A = permutedims(A, (1,3,2,4))
    A = reshape(A, (N^2, N^2))
    copy(A)
end

N = 10; D = 0.1
A = sprand(ComplexF64, N^2, N^2, D)
B = Matrix(A)
```

This pull request introduces significant restructuring and updates to the audio streaming project. The changes include the removal of outdated files, the addition of new documentation, and updates to the Dockerfile to streamline dependencies and improve the project setup. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### Removed Files and Documentation
* `AUDIO_SERVER_README.md`, `README.md`, `Validate.md`, and `audio_client.py`: These files were removed, indicating a shift in the project's focus and structure. The removed files included outdated documentation, validation checklists, and an audio client implementation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-71ade87a1f88d227305a22a43d9db9bd4ba904b7b7613d81256936f7b3269be2L1-L60) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L1-L132) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-22ae73f1f5ba26be94056b3ae53c9682e44abd7aed68eb7659655e194b800d92L1-L9) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b8c7692f0a8cb582bef9846fc0597ca689a484e16e1b259ba47bc67693011e47L1-L192)

* [`Dockerfile`](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557L5-R33): Simplified system dependencies by removing `portaudio19-dev` and unnecessary build tools, added directories for logs and recordings, and updated the command to run `server.py` instead of `audio_server.py`. This reflects a move to a more streamlined and updated server implementation.

* [`WebRTC_Client_Explanation.md`](diffhunk://#diff-b3e9613d9539874336888ac9a96b7c2e598eab8c5074bd83015b8f86d02ff29aR1-R71): Added a detailed explanation of the WebRTC client, covering audio capture, playback, processing, and connection management. body:
## What
Fix the ListItem and ContentValues streams that have errors when attempting to fetch certain records.

## How
They were doing a Cartesian product "Lists" X "Items", no matter if the `item` didn't belong to the `List`, which was leading to errors like:

```
columnvalues: MessageRepresentationAirbyteTracedErrors('\'GET\' request to \'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/site-id/lists/list-id/items/item-id?expand=fields\' failed with status code \'404\' and error message: \'The specified list item was not found\'. Request (body): \'None\'. Response (body): \'{\'error\': {\'code\': \'itemNotFound\', \'message\': \'The specified list item was not found\', ...
```

We are also adding FAST aribyte standard tests.

Users can nos sync these streams without errors

author: yue-zhengyuan
body: This PR implements rotations `rotl90`, `rotr90` and `rot180` for `InfiniteWeightPEPS` and `SUWeight`. In addition, we now restrict the virtual arrow directions in an `InfiniteWeightPEPS` to be either downward or leftward for easier operations in simple update algorithms. As a result, the arrow directions in an `InfiniteWeightPEPS` will not rotate together with the state.

author: csl-beta
body:
This PR adds comprehensive unit tests for two important game systems:

## New Test Classes
1. **AudioManagerTests**: Tests for the AudioManager class including:
   - Volume control and mute functionality
   - Noise type selection
   - Static noise generation and playback
   - Signal tone generation and playback
   - Squelch effects
   - Sound effect playback
   - Process method functionality
   - Noise generation methods

2. **GameProgressionManagerTests**: Tests for the GameProgressionManager class including:
   - Getting and setting progression stages
   - Advancing progression
   - Checking progression requirements
   - Getting stage descriptions and objectives
   - Progression to endgame
   - Progression events

## Benefits
- Improves test coverage for core game systems
- Verifies that audio functionality works correctly
- Ensures game progression mechanics function as expected
- Tests edge cases and error handling
- Provides documentation for expected behavior
- Makes the codebase more maintainable

These tests build on the existing test framework and help ensure that these critical systems work correctly. They follow the same patterns as our other unit tests, making them easy to understand and maintain.

author: thedarkcolour
body:
Backports the fix for https://github.com/thedarkcolour/ForestryCE/issues/207 to 1.7.10, which is a bug where Alveary blocks with separate inventories such as the Alveary Sieve do not drop their inventories when destroyed.

Adds an interface, `IMultiblockComponent.HasInventory`, which can be implemented on `IMultiblockComponent` to tell `BlockStructure` that it has a separate inventory from the rest of the multiblock (ex. the slot for Woven Silk on the Alveary Sieve) that should be dropped when the block is broken.

I found this because I was curious about whether the bug was a regression in my 1.20.1 version of Forestry, but found that the 1.7.10 also suffered from this bug.

Addon mods such as Binnie's might also need fixing, separately from this PR.

author: masnesral
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #151757
* #151749

Summary: The main motivation is to capture the cudagraphs overhead in a WaitCounter. We'll combine that with Triton autotuning, and therefore rename to "compile_runtime_overheads". Since we have a couple WaitCounters where we want to capture all runtime and compile overheads, let's put the accounting in dynamo_timed so we'll automatically capture any toplevel timed regions that get added in the future. Also, dynamo_timed already has to figure out if we're timing a runtime vs. compile-time event, so we can reuse some of that logic.

Test Plan:
Ran an internal model with `TORCHINDUCTOR_BENCHMARK_FUSION=1` (to get benchmarking at compile time in addition to runtime).

Overall compile time from various sources matches up:
* tlparse: https://fburl.com/9fgsstkr. Eyeballing, total time should be 32 ranks x 2175 = ~69.6k s
* ods: https://fburl.com/canvas/r4clhnb7. Right on.
* dynamo_compile: https://fburl.com/scuba/dynamo_compile/ax71aqox. Right on.
* pt2_compile_events: https://fburl.com/scuba/pt2_compile_events/shcjd9ql. Right on.

And the runtime overhead:
* ods: https://fburl.com/canvas/nvgjb282
* dynamo_compile: https://fburl.com/scuba/dynamo_compile/f2dtv0qh

If we compare that to a run of the same model without the changes in this stack, results can mismatch by a lot:
* tlparse: https://fburl.com/cchxwd1s. Eyeballing, total time should be 32 ranks x 2300s = ~73.5k s
* ods: https://fburl.com/canvas/x1i3wvf4. It's kinda close
* dynamo_compile: https://fburl.com/scuba/dynamo_compile/l7sgxdxd. Waaay too high.
* pt2_compile_events: https://fburl.com/scuba/pt2_compile_events/jb4s9z1u. This is the only one that's actually correct.

The discrepancy is even worse if we focus on the runtime events:
* ods: https://fburl.com/canvas/a4o9f7ou
* dynamo_compile: https://fburl.com/scuba/dynamo_compile/95izaes1

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change hardens all instances of [Runtime#exec()](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/Runtime.html) to offer protection against attack.

Left unchecked, `Runtime#exec()` can execute any arbitrary system command. If an attacker can control part of the strings used to as program paths or arguments, they could execute arbitrary programs, install malware, and anything else they could do if they had a shell open on the application host.

Our change introduces a sandbox which protects the application:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.SystemCommand;
  ...
- Process p = Runtime.getRuntime().exec(command);
+ Process p = SystemCommand.runCommand(Runtime.getRuntime(), command);
```

The default restrictions applied are the following:
* **Prevent command chaining**. Many exploits work by injecting command separators and causing the shell to interpret a second, malicious command. The `SystemCommand#runCommand()` attempts to parse the given command, and throw a `SecurityException` if multiple commands are present.
* **Prevent arguments targeting sensitive files.** There is little reason for custom code to target sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd`, so the sandbox prevents arguments that point to these files that may be targets for exfiltration.

There are [more options for sandboxing](https://github.com/pixee/java-security-toolkit/blob/main/src/main/java/io/github/pixee/security/SystemCommand.java#L15) if you are interested in locking down system commands even more.

body:
Just found this bug when investigating strange behavior of [this issue](https://github.com/DragonsPlusMinecraft/CreateEnchantmentIndustry/issues/253).

When a Item has no emptying recipe and also has `ForgeCapabilities.FLUID_HANDLER_ITEM/Capabilities.FluidHandler.ITEM`, `GenericItemEmptying#emptyItem` will get capability to obtain result. The key problem is: You cannot obtain correct result from `IFluidHandlerItem#getContainer` when `IFluidHandlerItem#drain` pass-in FluidAction parameter is `FluidAction.SIMULATE`.

So here is the fix: always pass in `FluidAction.EXECUTE`. It's OK to always pass in `FluidAction.EXECUTE` even when simulating, since we have copied the original ItemStack.
```
ItemStack split = stack.copy();
IFluidHandlerItem capability = split.getCapability(Capabilities.FluidHandler.ITEM);
resultingFluid = capability.drain(...
```

author: truongminhphung
body:
This pull request introduces a local development setup for testing AWS Lambda functions and APIs using SAM (Serverless Application Model) and refactors the backend utility codebase. Key changes include the addition of a CloudFormation template for local resources, updates to the Makefile for local development commands, and the creation of modularized utility components. 

### Local Development Setup
* Added `template-local.yaml` in `CloudFormation/dev_yaml` to define local AWS Lambda layers (`LocalPythonLayer`, `LocalLambdaCommonLayer`) and a `LoginFunction` for testing the `/task-management/login` API endpoint.
* Updated `Makefile` with commands for building and running the local SAM environment and updating Python dependencies.

### Backend Refactoring
#### Modularized Utility Components
* Moved and renamed utility files under `WebApp/backend/commonUtil/python/commonUtil` for better organization. Updated imports in affected files to reflect the new structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fcef85343d740a8fa5ec7febcbcb4c6a4d553ae91166c3f9597e76a3fa30e2ecL3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3b4f9d15ecbbfd83104514e154268ea0c0591fd55c5f63f2856ba8bad9d94576L2-R3)
* Added `config.py` to centralize environment-based configurations, including database connection strings and JWT secrets.
* Created `app_constants.py` to define reusable application-specific constants like JWT expiration time and validation rules.
* Added `error_messages.py` for centralized error messages and `http_status.py` for HTTP status code mappings. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2b892dee93b8afe8b508fd1bfc06882864fca72d03bc7358829acb1409a8a3c0R1-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-928b9322a3cd312acc59aca69455e4597bc35aa4821d7447b2b477fc2d9aa059R1-R18)

#### Database Utilities
* Added `db.py` with functions for establishing and managing PostgreSQL database connections using a context manager.

author: bkono
body:
Large run of changes here. Doc comments are present for each of the following new actions covering them in detail:

- `list`: returns the names of mailboxes that match the given pattern
- `capabilities`: A list of capabilities supported by the server
- `has_capability?`: Check of specific server support for a capability
- `move`: Move messages from current mailbox to a destination mailbox
- `create`: Create a new mailbox (aka folder)
- `fetch`: Fetches prior messages based on a sequence set. Messages are delivered to all subscribers just like new messages.

Also includes a few bug fixes and adjustments necessary to support the additional commands. 

I realize it's a fairly large PR, so this isn't a scope of features you want to merge, no worries. Or if you'd like some API related changes, let me know.

author: gejq21
body:
## Motivation

Support V2PE in pre-training, fine-tuning, and inference for InternVL.

## Modification

### V2PE utils

Added the file `internvl_chat/internvl/v2pe_utils.py`.  
It includes the `get_rope_pos_id` function, which calculates position ids required for V2PE,  
and a `V2PE` module that can replace the conventional RoPE mechanism.

### Pre-training and Fine-tuning

Modified the following files to support V2PE in training and fine-tuning:

- `internvl_chat/internvl/train/internvl_chat_pretrain.py`
- `internvl_chat/internvl/train/internvl_chat_finetune.py`

Specifically:
- Extended `ModelArguments` and `LazySupervisedDataset` to support V2PE.
- Updated `concat_pad_data_collator` in `internvl_chat/internvl/patch/pad_data_collator.py`  
  to support passing position ids as lists (to preserve float precision when using V2PE).

### Model

#### InternVLChat

- Modified `internvl_chat/internvl/model/internvl_chat/configuration_internvl_chat.py`  
  to support passing V2PE-related arguments via config.
- Updated `InternVLChatModel.forward()` and `InternVLChatModel.chat()`  
  in `internvl_chat/internvl/model/internvl_chat/modeling_internvl_chat.py`  
  to support V2PE usage during both training and inference.

#### InternLM2

- Modified `internvl_chat/internvl/model/internlm2/configuration_internlm2.py`  
  to support V2PE-related config arguments.
- Updated `InternLM2Attention._init_rope()`, `InternLM2Attention.forward()`,  
  and `InternLM2FlashAttention2.forward()` in  
  `internvl_chat/internvl/model/internlm2/modeling_internlm2.py`  
  to support replacing RoPE with the V2PE module.

body:
### General:

-   [ ] The pull request title is descriptive. _(ex. `Added Lunar Network`, not `Updated metadata.json`)_
-   [ ] The pull request does not contain any unrelated commits. _(ex. commits from previous pull requests)_

### Mapping Additions or Updates:

-   [ ] Folder with appropriate name has been created / updated (must not include any non-alpha characters or whitespace).
-   [ ] No changes were made to the file's formatting (4 spaces per tab).
-   [ ] There are no syntax errors.
-   [ ] There is no pre-existing mapping matching my id (check if there is an existing folder).
-   [ ] My field values match your requirements.
-   You can view our patterns here: [metadata.schema.json](https://github.com/LunarClient/ServerMappings/blob/master/metadata.schema.json), or take a look below and complete the field checklist:
    -   [ ] `id`: a lowercase string, which should match the folder name _(ex. `myserver`)_
    -   [ ] `name`: a string _(ex. `MyServerPvP`)_
    -   [ ] `description`: hook between 16 and 80 characters in English _(ex. `Home of Competitive Minecraft PvP`)_
    -   [ ] `addresses`: an array with lowercase strings _(ex. `["my.server", "your-server.com"]`)_
        -   You do not need to specify subdomains, Lunar Client services automatically detect them.
    -   [ ] `primaryAddress`: the primary address that people connect to with (please include the subdomain if required) _(ex. `mc.my.server`)_
    -   [ ] `minecraftVersions`: an array with Minecraft versions as strings _(ex. `["1.18._", "1.19.2"]` - Must be versions or subversions supported by Lunar Client)\*
    -   [ ] `primaryMinecraftVersion`: a Minecraft version as a string _(ex. `1.19.2` - Must be a subversion supported by Lunar Client)_
    -   [ ] `primaryColor`: a hexademical color code that primarily distinguishes the server _(ex. `#00FFFF`)_
    -   [ ] `secondaryColor`: a hexademical color code that accompanies the `primaryColor` of the server _(ex. `#FF0000`)_
    -   [ ] `primaryRegion`: the primary region where your server operates in _(ex. `NA`)_
    -   [ ] `regions`: a list of regions where you have servers located that service your players _(ex. `["NA", "EU", "AS"]`)_
    -   [ ] `gameTypes`: a list of games that describe the content on your server, must be a max of 3 listed _(ez. `["PVP", "UHC", "HCF"]`)_
    -   [ ] `crossplay`: whether the server has support for Bedrock Edition players (through proxies such as [GeyserMC](https://geysermc.org/))
    -   [ ] (optional) `presentationVideo`: YouTube video ID (in slug) to server trailer / introduction _(ex. `7EV4cPuJvXE`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `votingLinks`: an array of urls to your server's listing on voting websites _(ex. `["https://minecraft-mp.com/server-s179012"]`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `website`: url of server website, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://www.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `store`: url of server store, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://store.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `wiki`: url of server wiki, must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://wiki.your-server.com`)_
    -   [ ] (optional) `merch`: url of server merchanise site (if seperate from store), must include URL schema (http:// or https://) _(ex. `https://merch.your-server.com`)_

### Socials

-   [ ] (optional) `twitter`: username of twitter account without the @ _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `discord`: invite link to discord _(ex. https://discord.com/invite/4ceEJuH)_
-   [ ] (optional) `youtube`: slug or username of youtube channel _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `instagram`: username of instagram account _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `twitch`: username of twitch account _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `telegram`: slug of telegram group _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `reddit`: slug of subdreddit wtih 'r/' _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `tiktok`: username of tiktok account _(ex. MyServer)_
-   [ ] (optional) `facebook`: slug of facebook page _(ex. MyServer)_

### Compliance

-   [ ] (optional) `privacyPolicy`: url to your Privacy Policy _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/privacy)_
-   [ ] (optional) `termsOfService`: url to your Terms of Service _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/terms)_
-   [ ] (optional) `rules`: url to your Rules _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/rules)_
-   [ ] (optional) `support`: url to your Support Site _(ex. https://www.lunar.gg/support)_

### Media:

#### Logo

-   [ ] My logo is a `png` file.
-   [ ] I have uploaded my logo to my server folder _(ex. `lunarnetwork`)_ and named it `logo.png`.
-   [ ] My logo has a transparent background and is square (1:1 aspect ratio).
-   [ ] My logo is at least `512` pixels in width and height.
-   [ ] My logo is my own property and complies with relevant copyright/privacy laws.
-   [ ] My logo is not upscaled from a smaller low quality image.

#### Background

-   [ ] My background is a `png` file.
-   [ ] I have uploaded my background to my server folder _(ex. `lunarnetwork`)_ and named it `background.png`.
-   [ ] My background has an aspect ratio of 16:9.
-   [ ] My background is atleast `1920` pixels in width and `1080` pixels in height (can be bigger, but must remain the same aspect ratio).
-   [ ] My background contains relevant content pertaining to the server, is my own property, and complies with relevant copyright/privacy laws.
-   [ ] My background doesn't contain any markings, text, or logos (unless part of a build).

body:
<!-- Write **BELOW** The Headers and **ABOVE** The comments else it may not be viewable. -->

## About The Pull Request
Restructures all the slap crafting food interactions into datums
This allows us to have recipe datums referenced twice when the interaction is reverse without having to bring up the issue of manually writing attackbys for the slap craft objects. I tried to comment everything in case anyone in the future reads this and has no idea what it is (That person will be me)

### - Some info -
Recipes datums are laid out in the following way.
It has variables for:
-how long it takes to assemble (time_to_make)
- items used
- reagents (possibly for a future check, it's a remnant from my older code)
- the item you make (result)
- interaction type (this is so the datum can fire and know the difference between attackby and attackhand)
- slices (currently unused)
- sound to make on assembly (craft_sound)
- message to send to user (crafting_meesage)

They have the current procs:
**clear_items**
-  While loops through all the items in the recipe and qdels them from the world

**check_items_in_list**
- Creates an associated list and counts backwards to know you have enough items to actually make the recipe

**pre_check**
-  Simple proc you can use as a simple check for any special code a recipe might need (e.g. the peppermill needing to have reagents inside it to be used)
- Can be, and should be, overridden for these special cases

**post_handle**
-  Proc for anything that needs to happen after creation that is unique to that recipe (e.g. actually removing the reagent from the peppermill)

Adds the following global procs:
**select_interaction_recipe**
The real meat of this systems. Takes all the available recipes in the food interaction list, the items you want to check, the interaction type, and whether this is exact (it always is for now).

- Checks if you have enough items via check_items_in_list
- checks for the interaction type
- Runs through every recipe with these requirements
- Once it has a list it attempts to do the most complex recipe it can (AKA the one with most ingredients). Considering that most things are still 2 ingredients at most this wont matter for now but in the future it might mean you could say make a cake and skip the butterdough step if you have an egg also in you hand (provided it is written).

**food_handle_interaction**
Takes the source, user, items, and interaction type.
- Tries to find the recipe via previous proc
- Failure returns false (attackby and attack hand will call parent proc on failures)
- if it finds one it uses all the information from it to handle the actual making of the thing and then calls all the recipe's procs to clean up.


Attackby has changed for all `snacks` subtypes
- Looks for a table (currently all actions require a table)
- Attempts slice code first (I don't want to touch this yet and I don't think I have to)
- if slicing does not work we get a list of the player's holding items (active + inactive)
- add this to a list of to_check items with the original item hit.
- feed this into the previous proc to check
- on success we get a new meal / item
- on failure we try to call parent procs as a fallback.

attack_hand has changed for all `snacks` subtypes
- Find a table, if no table call parent proc
- if there is a table try the recipe interaction
- if the recipe fails try the parent proc.

Adds two defines for the interaction types 
`#define FOOD_INTERACTION_ITEM 1 // use for attackby proc`
`#define FOOD_INTERACTION_HAND 2 // use for attack_hand proc`

I think those are the only three things I gotta fix. I can do those after I get this PR posted up.

### UPDATE: 2025/05/19
**Cooking from Scratch (Lucky Lily)**
Adds:

- Venus cake (cake base + jacksberries)
- fruitcake (base + apples + berries (hold two in your hands, click third))
- plain cake (bake base)
- iced cake (base + sugar)
- fish fillet (cut again for mince)
- scalloped potatoes (fried potatoes + cheese wedge)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9582b1c5-8cfe-4b0a-99ef-22caa05e5eae)

<!-- Describe The Pull Request. Please be sure every change is documented or this can delay review and even discourage maintainers from merging your PR! -->

## Why It's Good For The Game
Ideally if everything is working the players should notice absolutely no difference in how cooking currently works. So from a user end experience this changes nothing.

However from a dev perspective this should allow making food slap crafting a lot more concise and clear as you now only need to list the items you want to use (1-3 of them) make a small pre_check proc for any special edge cases and then you no longer have to worry about inconsistent items not having matching attackby logic (e.g. currently a chicken cutlet onto fried potatoes will show message but the inverse does not.)

It may also help references in the future if say books want to keep a list of recipes, now it wont have to be manual because you could just load this whole datum into the book and save it there.

<!-- Argue for the merits of your changes and how they benefit the game, especially if they are controversial and/or far reaching. If you can't actually explain WHY what you are doing will improve the game, then it probably isn't good for the game in the first place. -->
## Proof of Testing (Required)
Me trying to make every recipe I could think of (they all seemed to work)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/977d14e7-c29b-4bed-952f-bf642f5bbbc6

example of wiener meal being made in either order
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ca38574-ac4f-4b0c-96cd-e8638a809c5b

Example of extra items not being eaten by code.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e86740de-7417-4be5-a41b-1af498255a2b

Added core security utilities to `@shadow-dev/core/security`, including:
- Password hashing and verification using Argon2id
- JWT token signing and verification with configurable expiry
- Secure token and API key generation
- HMAC signing and verification with timing-safe comparison

These utilities provide reusable, security-focused primitives for use across all ShadowDev projects, including ShadowVault and future panel work.

   const hash = await hashPassword('test123');
   const valid = await verifyPassword('test123', hash);
   ```
3. Verify HMAC signing works:

   const sig = signHMAC("payload", "secret");

- **Pledged $1000:** The company has _promised_ to give $1000, but has not necessarily given it yet. It's a commitment for the future.
- **Contributed $1000:** The company has _actually given_ $1000 already. The money has been transferred or donated.


In short:
- Pledge = promise (future)
- Contribute = action done (completed)

body:
According to the notes, we start by importing rospy, and then we import our custom message from the packag
We first create a subscriber node (the listener) where we define a callback function. This function starts working every time a new bot position message is received. Inside the callback, we use rospy.loginfo() to display the bot’s position in the format (x, y, direction).
Then, we create a publisher node where the user enters movement commands like forward, left,  right....
We maintain a  track on the bot’s current x, y position and its direction. Based on the command entered, we update these variables accordingly.
After updating the position, we publish a bot position message with the new x, y, and direction.
We use rospy.sleep(n) so that there is a time lag of n sec
The if_name == '_main_' thing is the default as provided in the notes.

body:
There’s currently no return or raise in `PrinterInterface::get_state_id`, this patch simply adds in a rais NotImplementError() like the other methods to stop the interpretter/type checker being upset.  Because I was touching the function, I also threw on a `-> str` to document the return type.

Tested by verifying that the type checker no longer complains about functions that call get_state_id expecting to get a str back, and some basic "does it still run/pass the unit tests".

author: chriscrl
body:
Prepare Models for Periodic Notification System Implementation
---

## **Overview**  
### **What does this PR do?**  
This PR establishes the foundational model changes needed for our upcoming Celery-based notification system. It modifies the existing Notification model to include priority levels, updates the Lesson model with reminder fields, and introduces a new Session model to track tutoring sessions.

---

## **Key Features & Changes**  
**Model Enhancements**: Added priority field to the Notification model  
**New Model Creation**: Implemented Session model for tracking tutoring sessions  
**Model Updates**: Added reminder tracking to the Assignment model  

- Added priority field (`low`, `medium`, `high`) to `Notification` model
- Created new `Session` model with fields for tracking tutoring sessions
- Modified existing `Assignment` model to support reminder functionality
- Prepared all necessary models for upcoming Celery task implementation

---

## **Why This Is Needed**  
### **What problem does this solve?**  
This PR lays the groundwork for our notification system by establishing the data structures necessary to track sessions, assignments, and notification priorities. 

---

## **Related Issue**  
🔗 **This PR addresses** Issue #164 (which is a sub-issue of main Issue #50)

---

## **Implementation Details**  
### **How was this feature developed?**  
- Added a `priority` field to the `Notification` model with `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, and `HIGH` choices
- Created a new `Session` model with:
  - References to student and tutor profiles
  - Session timing details
  - Location information
  - Status tracking
  - Reminder tracking
- Updated the `Assignment` model with a `reminder_sent` field

---

## **How to Test This PR**  
### **Step-by-step testing guide**  
1️⃣ Run migrations to create the new models and fields  
2️⃣ Access Django admin to verify the Notification model's new priority field  
3️⃣ Create a test Session through the admin interface  
4️⃣ Verify that relationships between models work correctly  

---

author: voodoohop
body:
## Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive GitHub authentication system for Pollinations services that follows the "thin proxy" design principle. The implementation provides users with two authentication options:

1. **Referrer-based authentication** - Automatically authenticate based on whitelisted domains
2. **Token-based authentication** - Provide users with a personal access token they can use directly

## Key Components

### MCP Integration
- Added GitHub authentication tools to the MCP server
- Created schema definitions for GitHub tools
- Implemented service functions following the thin proxy pattern

### Authentication System
- Implemented GitHub OAuth flow with session management
- Created JSON-based token storage for user tokens and referrers
- Added endpoints for token and referrer management

### API Endpoints
- `/github/login` - Start OAuth flow
- `/github/callback` - Handle GitHub redirect with auth code
- `/github/status` - Check authentication status
- `/github/token` - Get or regenerate Pollinations token
- `/github/referrers/*` - Manage authorized referrers

## Implementation Details

The implementation follows the modular architecture pattern used in the Pollinations MCP server:

1. **GitHub Schema** (`model-context-protocol/src/services/githubSchema.js`)
   - Defines tool schemas for GitHub authentication capabilities
   - Follows the modular pattern of existing schema files

2. **GitHub Service** (`model-context-protocol/src/services/githubService.js`)
   - Implements thin proxy functions for GitHub authentication
   - Provides simple, direct interfaces for auth operations

3. **Token Storage** (`text.pollinations.ai/github/tokenStorage.js`)
   - JSON-based storage for user tokens and referrers
   - Clean, minimal API for token management

4. **GitHub Auth Core** (`text.pollinations.ai/github/githubAuth.js`)
   - Implements GitHub OAuth flow with session management
   - Follows standard OAuth best practices

5. **GitHub Routes** (`text.pollinations.ai/github/githubRoutes.js`)
   - Express routes for all GitHub authentication endpoints
   - Simple, RESTful API design

## Testing

To test this implementation:

1. Set the required environment variables:
   ```
   GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=your_github_client_id
   GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=your_github_client_secret
   GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI=https://text.pollinations.ai/github/callback
   ```

2. Start the text.pollinations.ai server
3. Visit `/github/login` to initiate the OAuth flow
4. After authentication, use the provided session ID for API calls

## Future Extensions

This authentication system is designed to form the foundation for future user management capabilities, including the user subdomain management system described in issue #1738.

Closes #1737

author: frankfurter123
body: ## Add Role-Based Questionnaire Flow Post-Login ### Overview This PR introduces a full **role-based onboarding questionnaire** that appears right after login for new users (students and tutors). The modal-style component collects key info like contact preferences, school details, and tutor subjects, allowing us to store meaningful data based on role — all before they hit the dashboard. It also includes updated UI polish, conditional logic (e.g. show email/phone fields based on choice), tutor-specific fields like hourly rate and subjects, and a confetti effect to celebrate completion. ---------- ### Key Features & Changes ✔ **Core Feature Implementation**: - Added a modal-based multi-step questionnaire component that appears after login, driven by `userRole`. - Includes separate paths for students (school type, emergency contact, etc.) and tutors (bio, hourly rate, subjects). - Uses conditional rendering for sub-fields like grade level and contact method. ✔ **UI/UX Enhancements**: - Added confetti celebration on final submission 🎉 - Styled subject checkboxes in a responsive grid for tutors - Added helpful placeholders for all major input fields (email, phone, city, etc.) - Hourly rate input supports a clean `$` prefix while storing raw number behind the scenes. ✔ **State Management**: - All form steps are state-driven with `useState` - Step logic supports 3 questions per page and adapts dynamically based on answers - LocalStorage used to track completion (`questionnaireCompleted`) so modal doesn't repeat ✔ **New Components/Files**: - `Questionnaire.jsx`: handles role switching, rendering logic, form steps, and submission - `Questionnaire.css`: all layout, spacing, and styling for form, checkboxes, modal, and confetti - Assets reused from existing theme — no new images added ---------- ### Why This Is Needed Before this, users landed directly on the dashboard without completing any profile-specific info. This questionnaire ensures we gather key data early in a structured way, helping us tailor the platform experience based on role and improving backend data integrity. ---------- ### Related Issue 🔗 This PR addresses issue #165 ---------- ### Implementation Details - Built using React (`useState` + `useEffect`) - Conditionally renders fields based on answers using simple branching logic - Tracks user progress through steps and shows visual feedback - Tutor subject selection supports checkbox grids with optional custom input - Final screen triggers confetti and calls `onComplete()` callback ---------- ### Design Documentation ✔ **Tutor View Prompt questions**: Part 1 : Part 2 : ✔ **Student View Prompt questions**: Part 1 (By Email) : Part 1 (By phone) : Part 2 (College Student) : Part 2 (HighSchool Student) : Part 3: Part 4 (confetti): ---------- ### UML Diagram ![role_based_questionnaire_flow](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/423c9f98-4d93-40aa-8896-5c4a84edbee2) ---------- ### How to Test This PR 1️⃣ Log in with a fresh student or tutor account 2️⃣ Questionnaire modal should appear automatically 3️⃣ Fill out each step — should show 3 questions per page 4️⃣ Select "Phone" or "Email" → additional fields should appear 5️⃣ For students, selecting "college" or "high school" should show grade level 6️⃣ For tutors, the subject selection grid should appear 7️⃣ Submit the form → confetti should display and modal should close 8️⃣ Refresh the page — modal should **not** reappear (completion saved in localStorage) ---------- ### 📂 Files Added/Modified | File Path | Description | |----------------------------------|----------------------------------------| | frontend/src/Components/Questionnaire.jsx | Main component for post-login onboarding flow | | frontend/src/Styles/Questionnaire.css | Styling for the questionnaire modal and inputs | | frontend/src/Components/StudentView.jsx | Integrated Questionnaire for student role | | frontend/src/Components/TutorView.jsx | Integrated Questionnaire for tutor role | | frontend/src/App.jsx | Passes userRole and handles routing post-login | ---------- ### 🤖 AI Code Usage No — all logic and UI built manually. ---------- ### ✅ Checklist for Reviewers - [ ] Does the modal appear correctly post-login based on role? - [ ] Are 3 questions shown per step, with clean transitions? - [ ] Do conditional fields render and behave as expected? - [ ] Is tutor subject selection working with the checkbox grid? - [ ] Is the UI responsive and confetti firing on submit? - [ ] Does localStorage correctly prevent re-showing modal? ---------- ### 📈 Next Steps & Future Enhancements - Connect questionnaire to backend API to save profile data - Add Parent role support with its own flow - Save responses in DB for persistence across sessions - Optionally allow users to return and edit questionnaire later - Accessibility review and keyboard nav improvements ---------- ### Final Notes Thanks for reviewing! Let me know if you spot anything off — happy to clean it up further. This lays a strong foundation for role-based onboarding and gets us one step closer to a polished student/tutor experience. After merging this PR, implementing back end should be so much easier. — Franklin

author: ctiller
body:
Previously channelz kept an index of all objects in a global std::map protected by a single mutex.

Instead: split the index in two. The first is a list of all base nodes, queryable on demand, sharded by pointer. These base nodes are available, but un-numbered. The id allocation then occurs whenever channelz is actually queried. At that point unnumbered nodes can be iterated and numbered sequentially, keeping that essential invariant for channelz pagination.

In doing so, most nodes never need to hit a singleton global resource at all: the most they do is take a sharded lock and do a list insert/removal pair.

(it turns out this code is a major source of contention in gRPC)

Add a soda machine, which spawns in the same locations as food processors as well as an atomic soda machine that can craft atomic energy drinks akin to the atomic coffeepot. (currently looks the same too) New CO2 canisters are used to fuel it.
Carbonated beverages can be crafted with sugar, water, some sort of flavor item, and sometimes caffeine.

orange soda syrup

grape soda syrup
root beer syrup
dark cola syrup

energy dew syrup

can all be found at restaurant locations

can be found at military locations

bag in a box container

suicide mixed drink

additional recipes:
pine needle soda (carbonated pine needle tea)

Ensured item spawns as expected and player can craft normal soda recipes using the soda machine and atomic soda machine. 
Confirmed atomic soda machine can craft atomic energy drinks, the soda equivalent of atomic coffee.

body: Copied from -> https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/2141 NOTE: Making a separate PR was easier than overwriting the original PR but once this is merged I will give them credit. ### Description(copied from the PR) This PR prevents file editing tools (`write_to_file` and `replace_in_file`) from being used in PLAN mode. I understand that PLAN mode is intended for information gathering and planning purposes, while actual execution like file editing should be done in ACT mode. This is because PLAN mode is specifically designed for "planning" as opposed to "acting" in ACT mode, with clear role separation between the two. In the current implementation, file editing tools can still be used in PLAN mode, which is inconsistent with the mode's intended purpose. I noticed this issue, and after seeing that other users had mentioned similar concerns in #1621 #2024, I decided to implement this fix. This PR adds the necessary checks to enforce this restriction and updates the system prompt to explicitly state this limitation, ensuring that the system behavior matches the intended purpose of PLAN mode. ### Test Procedure I tested this by: 1. Switching to PLAN mode 2. Attempting to use file editing tools 3. Verifying that the appropriate error message is displayed ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6f344c8-cbbc-45e3-961e-9704558964f1) This change is minimal and focused on a specific condition check, so the risk of introducing bugs is low. Part of MOT-113
This pull request introduces a new `DependencyElements` class for generating Spring Boot project configuration files and adds corresponding unit tests. The most important changes include implementing the `DependencyElements` class, creating a Jinja2 template for `build.gradle.kts`, and adding test cases to validate the new functionality.

### New Feature: Spring Boot Dependency Management

* **`DependencyElements` class added**: A new class `DependencyElements` was created in `app/models/elements.py` to generate Spring Boot project configuration files using a Jinja2 template. It includes a method `print_django_style` (which should be renamed to `print_springboot_style`) for rendering the template with project-specific data.

* **Jinja2 template for `build.gradle.kts`**: Added a new template file `app/templates/springboot/build.gradle.kts.j2` to define the structure of the `build.gradle.kts` file. It dynamically incorporates dependencies, repositories, and project-specific settings.

### Testing Enhancements

* **Unit tests for `DependencyElements`**: Added a new test class `TestDependencyElements` in `tests/test_elements.py` to validate the functionality of the `DependencyElements` class. It includes positive, negative, and edge case tests for the `print_django_style` method.

* **Import update**: Updated imports in `tests/test_elements.py` to include the new `DependencyElements` class.

author: contem
body:
This PR improves the `compare()` function to correctly handle version strings that include suffixes such as `8.5p1`, `10.2a`, etc. These suffixes are commonly used in systems like OpenSSH.

### Before:
compare('8.5', '8.5p1'); // returned 0 (incorrect)

### After:
compare('8.5', '8.5p1'); // now returns -1 (correct)

### Changes:
- Enhanced `split()` to detect and separate numeric-alphabetic suffixes.
- Improved `convertToNumber()` to preserve alphas properly.
- Added sample test cases to `test.js` (optional).

Let me know if any changes are needed!

author: danebulat
body:
- [x] Fix nomination pool roles data
  Role addresses are encoded before being cached for use in the application, and can be compared correctly in the subscription callback. 

- [x] Fix data index registry
  The batch `subscribeTasks` method has been temporarily deprecated because of the data index registry being incorrectly built for query multi handling. Subscriptions are currently built one-by-one. This code should be optimised in a future PR. 

- [x] Fix offline app initialisation
  The main window initialises imported accounts and subscriptions correctly when the app starts offline.

- [x] Fix post subscription callback processing
  Managed account data is updated after all subscription callbacks have finished processing. Managed state was previously being updated within the callback itself, potentially invalidating subsequent callbacks that should have been processed.

body:
## Context
Experiments intended to improve model training and performance.

## Changes
- new custom combined loss -> `MSELoss` + `StructuralSimilarityIndexMeasure`
- increased initial lr + dynamically decreasing
- weight decay
- early training stopping
- skip connections
- remove `BatchNorm2d`
- deeper model
- `DenoisingAutoencoderMini` for local use and `DenoisingAutoencoder` for training on bigger instances

## Experiments
Increasing the depth of the model didn't bring any improvements, unless accompanied with an increase in the initial resizing. The main issue was that doubling the image dimension meant 4x more memory, so I went on to train on an external GPU powered compute. Below are the results:

Pink on BSDS300 dataset and green on a collection of 409 landscape images taken by me.

## Overview
This PR introduces a set of Clarity smart contracts for managing commercial lease administration on the blockchain. The system provides a transparent, immutable, and automated way to handle property verification, lease terms, rent escalation, and compliance tracking.

## Features
- **Property Verification Contract**: Validates ownership and property details
- **Lease Terms Contract**: Manages critical dates and lease obligations
- **Rent Escalation Contract**: Calculates rent increases based on agreed formulas
- **Compliance Tracking Contract**: Monitors adherence to lease covenants

## Technical Details
- All contracts are written in Clarity (.clar)
- Comprehensive test suite using Vitest
- Simple, focused implementation with clear separation of concerns

## Implementation Notes
- Each contract has a defined data structure with appropriate maps
- Public functions for creating, updating, and querying data
- Read-only functions for retrieving information
- Access control to ensure only authorized parties can perform certain actions

## Testing
Tests are implemented using Vitest and focus on verifying the functionality of each contract. The tests use mocks to simulate the blockchain environment without relying on external libraries.

This pull request introduces a new feature to support request interception when creating browser pages. The changes primarily involve passing a `requestInterceptor` function through the relevant methods and ensuring it is correctly applied to browser pages.

* [`index.js`](diffhunk://#diff-e727e4bdf3657fd1d798edcd6b099d6e092f8573cba266154583a746bba0f346R110-R118): Added a `requestInterceptor` parameter to the `createInstance` function, passing it along to the internal `createInstance` call.

If provided, it enables request interception on the browser page and attaches the interceptor function to the `request` event.

In the original code, using `await` inside each `readFile` call within `Promise.all` made them execute sequentially, negating the parallel execution benefit of `Promise.all`. The refactored version uses `.then` to parse JSON after `readFile` promises resolve, enabling all operations in `Promise.all` to run truly in parallel.

body:
# Overview 

- Unused dependencies removed
- Scalar library changed with native code

---

This pull request introduces significant updates to the OpenAPI Scalar integration, focusing on simplifying dependencies, improving the `ScalarReference` class, and enhancing configurability with a new type definition for API reference options. The most important changes include removing external dependencies, refactoring the `ScalarReference` class, and adding a comprehensive type definition for configuration options.

### Dependency Removal and Refactoring:
* Removed `@hono/zod-openapi` and `hono-openapi` dependencies from `deno.json`, streamlining the project's dependency tree.
* Removed the `apiReference` import from `@scalar/hono-api-reference` and replaced it with an inline HTML generation function in `ScalarReference`, eliminating reliance on external libraries. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-07a9dcd5cfdc0958da0206d50ed6f808b7d0b9fb36820212cc6fa01ee1198cadL1-R2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-07a9dcd5cfdc0958da0206d50ed6f808b7d0b9fb36820212cc6fa01ee1198cadL28-R61)

### ScalarReference Class Enhancements:
* Refactored the `ScalarReference` class to generate HTML directly using a new `getScalarHTML` function, improving performance and reducing external calls. The `getResponse` method now supports both synchronous and asynchronous responses.

### Configuration and Type Definitions:
* Added a new file, `scalar.type.ts`, defining a detailed `ApiReferenceOptions` type, including configuration options for themes, layouts, dark mode, and other customizable settings for the API reference.

### Codebase Organization:
* Updated `index.ts` to export the new `scalar.type.ts` file, ensuring the new type definitions are accessible throughout the project.

### Motivation / Background

<!--
Describe why this Pull Request needs to be merged. What bug have you fixed? What feature have you added? Why is it important?
If you are fixing a specific issue, include "Fixes #ISSUE" (replace with the issue number, remove the quotes) and the issue will be linked to this PR.
-->

Developers can use the `param_encoding` method to specify the character encoding for a parameter.  
However, it requires a one line for each parameter.  
This is tiresome for developers and may also lead to bugs if they forget to specify the encoding.

### Detail

This PR introduces the `default_parameter_encoding` method to simplify this.  
`default_parameter_encoding` allows specifying a default encoding for all parameters in a given action.
    
This enhancement makes the codebase of applications receiving non-UTF-8 encoded data cleaner and easier to maintain.

#### before
``` ruby
class FooController < ActionController::Base
  param_encoding :create, :japanese_string_param1, Encoding::SHIFT_JIS
  param_encoding :create, :japanese_string_param2, Encoding::SHIFT_JIS
  param_encoding :create, :japanese_string_param3, Encoding::SHIFT_JIS
  param_encoding :create, :japanese_string_param4, Encoding::SHIFT_JIS
  param_encoding :create, :japanese_string_param5, Encoding::SHIFT_JIS
  param_encoding :create, :japanese_string_param6, Encoding::SHIFT_JIS

  def create
    create_params = params.permit(
      :japanese_string_param1,
      :japanese_string_param2,
      :japanese_string_param3,
      :japanese_string_param4,
      :japanese_string_param5,
      :japanese_string_param6
    ).transform_values! { |param| param.encode(Encoding::UTF_8) }
    Foo.create!(create_params)
    head :ok
  end
end
```

#### after
``` ruby
class FooController < ActionController::Base
  default_parameter_encoding :create, Encoding::SHIFT_JIS

  def create
    create_params = params.permit(

## Proposed change
Some devices seem to give up when being requested too much. Given on earlier conversations with the manufactures, I believed it was a bug in some specific firmware that didn't free memory, but following [reference](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/142619#issuecomment-2802541122) mentions that we may be sending too many commands at the same time. 

Although documentaiton is sparse about it, I've set following vars to make it more acceptable although I'm not sure if it's correct to add. I haven't run into issues myself yet and I'm unable to time if it's only make one update every 5 seconds.

author: apstndb
body:
This PR introduces new `EXPLAIN` notation via spannerplanviz package.

- https://github.com/apstndb/spannerplanviz/releases/tag/v0.5.0
  - Now, `Full scan: true` metadata is shown as `Full scan`.
  - Now, `scan_target` metadata and `distribution_table` metadata are shown as `on <target>` after operator name.
- https://github.com/apstndb/spannerplanviz/releases/tag/v0.5.1
  - Fix to show `[Input]` pseudo link type in `* Apply` operators.
- `CLI_SPANNER_CLI_COMPATIBLE_PLAN=true` shows old notation.

## Breaking Change

- `CLI_EXECUTION_METHOD_FORMAT` (introduced by https://github.com/apstndb/spanner-mycli/pull/178, [v0.12.0](https://github.com/apstndb/spanner-mycli/releases/tag/v0.12.0)) is replaced by `CLI_SPANNER_CLI_COMPATIBLE_PLAN`.

## Example

```sql
SELECT *
FROM Singers@{FORCE_INDEX=SingersByFirstLastName}
WHERE FirstName = "Marc";
```
### Before
```
+-----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ID  | Query_Execution_Plan <execution_method> (metadata, ...)                                           |
+-----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  *0 | Distributed Union <Row> (distribution_table: SingersByFirstLastName, split_ranges_aligned: false) |
|  *1 | +- Distributed Cross Apply <Row>                                                                  |
|   2 |    +- Create Batch <Row>                                                                          |
|   3 |    |  +- Local Distributed Union <Row>                                                            |
|   4 |    |     +- Compute Struct <Row>                                                                  |
|   5 |    |        +- Filter Scan <Row> (seekable_key_size: 0)                                           |
|  *6 |    |           +- Index Scan <Row> (Index: SingersByFirstLastName, scan_method: Automatic)        |
|  17 |    +- [Map] Serialize Result <Row>                                                                |
|  18 |       +- Cross Apply <Row>                                                                        |
|  19 |          +- KeyRangeAccumulator <Row>                                                             |
|  20 |          |  +- Batch Scan <Row> (Batch: $v2, scan_method: Row)                                    |
|  23 |          +- [Map] Local Distributed Union <Row>                                                   |
|  24 |             +- Filter Scan <Row> (seekable_key_size: 0)                                           |
| *25 |                +- Table Scan <Row> (Table: Singers, scan_method: Row)                             |
+-----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
Predicates(identified by ID):
  0: Split Range: ($FirstName = 'Marc')
  1: Split Range: ($SingerId' = $SingerId)
  6: Seek Condition: IS_NOT_DISTINCT_FROM($FirstName, 'Marc')
 25: Seek Condition: ($SingerId' = $batched_SingerId)
```

### New Default

```
+-----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ID  | Query_Execution_Plan <execution_method> (metadata, ...)                               |
+-----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  *0 | Distributed Union on SingersByFirstLastName <Row> (split_ranges_aligned: false)       |
|  *1 | +- Distributed Cross Apply <Row>                                                      |
|   2 |    +- [Input] Create Batch <Row>                                                      |
|   3 |    |  +- Local Distributed Union <Row>                                                |
|   4 |    |     +- Compute Struct <Row>                                                      |
|   5 |    |        +- Filter Scan <Row> (seekable_key_size: 0)                               |
|  *6 |    |           +- Index Scan on SingersByFirstLastName <Row> (scan_method: Automatic) |
|  17 |    +- [Map] Serialize Result <Row>                                                    |
|  18 |       +- Cross Apply <Row>                                                            |
|  19 |          +- [Input] KeyRangeAccumulator <Row>                                         |
|  20 |          |  +- Batch Scan on $v2 <Row> (scan_method: Row)                             |
|  23 |          +- [Map] Local Distributed Union <Row>                                       |
|  24 |             +- Filter Scan <Row> (seekable_key_size: 0)                               |
| *25 |                +- Table Scan on Singers <Row> (scan_method: Row)                      |
+-----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
Predicates(identified by ID):
  0: Split Range: ($FirstName = 'Marc')
  1: Split Range: ($SingerId' = $SingerId)
  6: Seek Condition: IS_NOT_DISTINCT_FROM($FirstName, 'Marc')
 25: Seek Condition: ($SingerId' = $batched_SingerId)
```

author: incredimike
body:
The `MessageRequest::setRaw(array $data)` method requires one array parameter which is merged into the request array. The logic for when the "raw" data SHOULD be applied is up for debate, but currently it is after the messages, but before any other options are set by the library (e.g. setMaxTokens()), so those explicit methods will always overwrite the raw settings.

I added this method becuase I wanted to use Claude's "thinking" tool which required adding the "thinking" attribute to my request array. See https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-think-tool

I don't think the other services offer this "thinking" tool, so adding a setThinking() method to MessageRequest didn't seem to make sense...  Eventually I realized modifying the raw request array/JSON would be more convenient and leave the implementation of the thinking tool functionality to the package author.

author: adebanjohikmat
body:
## Overview
This PR implements the Facility Registration Contract, a core component of our decentralized commercial parking revenue management system. The contract enables parking facility owners to register, update, and manage their parking structures on the blockchain.

## Features
- **Facility Registration**: Allows owners to register new parking facilities with details including name, address, and total spaces
- **Facility Management**: Supports updating facility information and toggling active status
- **Ownership Controls**: Enforces that only the registered owner can modify facility details
- **Unique Identification**: Assigns a unique ID to each registered facility for reference in other contracts

## Implementation Details

### Data Structures
- `last-facility-id`: Tracks the most recently assigned facility ID
- `facilities` map: Stores facility details indexed by facility ID, including:
  - Name (string-ascii, max 100 chars)
  - Address (string-ascii, max 200 chars)
  - Total spaces (uint)
  - Owner (principal)
  - Active status (boolean)

### Key Functions
- `register-facility`: Creates a new facility entry with the caller as owner
- `update-facility`: Allows owner to modify facility details
- `deactivate-facility`: Allows owner to mark a facility as inactive
- `reactivate-facility`: Allows owner to reactivate a previously deactivated facility
- `get-facility`: Read-only function to retrieve facility details
- `get-last-facility-id`: Read-only function to get the most recent facility ID

### Error Handling
- Returns appropriate error codes for invalid operations:
  - `u1`: Invalid space count (must be > 0)
  - `u403`: Unauthorized (not the facility owner)
  - `u404`: Facility not found

## Testing
The implementation includes comprehensive tests that verify:
- Successful facility registration with valid parameters
- Rejection of invalid registration attempts (e.g., zero spaces)
- Owner-only access for update operations
- Proper activation/deactivation functionality
- Correct error handling for all edge cases

## Security Considerations
- All modification functions verify the caller is the registered facility owner
- Input validation prevents registration of facilities with invalid parameters
- No functions allow changing the ownership of a facility after registration

## Future Enhancements
- Add support for multiple owners/administrators per facility
- Implement facility transfer functionality with secure ownership handover
- Add metadata support for additional facility information (amenities, etc.)
- Implement tiered space types (standard, premium, accessible, etc.)

## Related Components
This contract will be used by:
- Rate Management Contract: To verify facility existence and ownership
- Payment Processing Contract: To validate payments against registered facilities
- Revenue Reconciliation Contract: To track utilization against registered capacity
```

I've created detailed PR documentation specifically for the Facility Registration Contract component of the parking management system. This PR details document:

1. Provides an overview of the contract's purpose
2. Lists all key features implemented
3. Explains the data structures and functions in detail
4. Documents the error handling approach
5. Outlines the testing strategy
6. Addresses security considerations
7. Suggests future enhancements
8. Shows how this contract relates to other components

This document would be ideal for a pull request that specifically implements or updates the facility registration functionality within the larger parking management system.

body:
---

### **Description**

This PR introduces a custom error handler to ensure all API error responses follow a standardized format. This allows API clients to consistently parse and handle errors across the application.

---

### **Error Response Format**

All error responses will adhere to the following structure:

```json
{
  "error_code": "error_code",  // A unique code identifying the error type
  "message": "Human-readable error message",  // A descriptive message for the error
  "http_status_code": "HTTP status code, e.g., 400",  // The HTTP status code associated with the error
  "metadata": {  // Optional field for additional error details
    // Key-value pairs providing more context about the error
  }
}
```

---

### **Example**

For the following request:

```bash
curl -X 'POST' \
  'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tasks' \
  -H 'accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-CSRFTOKEN: su2Ejw3aNXDHnOm3NhNyq8ZjrfGKXZNpIVXjbkxFJpbgg4TttO6BgzcDpzhyO5FR' \
  -d '{
  "description": "string",
  "completed": true
}'
```

The API will return the following error response:

```json
{
  "error_code": "validation_error",
  "message": "Given data is not valid.",
  "http_status_code": 400,
  "metadata": {
    "title": [
      "This field is required."
    ]
  }
}
```

---

### **Key Changes**
- Added a global exception handler to standardize error responses.
- Updated all existing exceptions to use the new format.
- Enhanced error metadata to provide additional context where applicable.

---

This PR ensures a consistent and predictable error-handling mechanism, improving the developer experience for API clients.

author: charlesra752
body:
Changes you need to make to run: 
- I've left it on chat, but basically all previous files should be in next-app, the .env should be moved to the new root (next to docker-compose.yml and outside of the next-app and nginx folders), and the DATABASE_URL="" should be @postgres:5432 instead of @localhost:5432.

New files: 
- Docker compose, docerfile for nginx and next-app, config files for nginx, and a new folder for next app

Other changes: 
- Moving the whole repository into the file / docker container for next-app
- Changed from bcrypt to bcryptjs in bug-fixes. It might be fine if you revert to bcrypt, I think I implemented more fixes than I needed to not knowing that I had to reboot docker. Some of the earlier fixes might have been enough. 

The Dockerfile for each image will tell you how that image builds, and the docker compose builds the whole application; it builds each image as a container and defines how they interact each other (the interactions are defined in the docker compose file). Each container can be built and run independently (so you can rebuild the app without having to rebuild the server and the database). 

There is information stored between builds, and this is in docker volumes (and there's the cache as well). I don't think we need to worry about that too much (except for build an updated version of our code without a cache, to make sure that we're not using old information)

This pull request introduces a new "Sign Up" feature to the application, including a dedicated signup page, navigation updates, and layout adjustments. The most significant changes involve adding the `SignupPage` component, updating routing and navigation, and enhancing the `AuthLayout` component to support the new page.

### New Signup Page Implementation:
* Added a new `SignupPage` component (`src/pages/auth/SignupPage.tsx`) with form validation using Formik and Yup, a terms and conditions checkbox, and Google sign-up button. The page is styled with `AuthLayout` and includes animations via `framer-motion`.

### Routing Updates:

body:
This pull request introduces changes to enhance the automation and documentation of Terraform modules in the repository. Key updates include enabling the `terraform_docs` pre-commit hook with custom configurations, adding a `.terraform-docs.yml` configuration file, and improving the `README.md` by integrating auto-generated documentation. Additionally, new examples and minor variable description updates have been included.

### Pre-commit Hook Enhancements:
* Enabled the `terraform_docs` pre-commit hook with custom configurations to exclude `examples/` and specify arguments for generating and injecting documentation into the `README.md` file.

### Documentation Improvements:
* Introduced a `.terraform-docs.yml` configuration file to define formatting, content structure, and output settings for generating Terraform module documentation. 
* Updated `README.md` to include placeholders for auto-generated Terraform documentation, such as inputs, outputs, providers, and resources. 

### Examples:
* Added a new example in `examples/primary/main.tf` to demonstrate the usage of the Terraform module, including configuration for workload projects. 

### Minor Updates:
* Clarified the description of the `environment` variable to specify its purpose for InfraWeave environments.

author: pelumi2282
body:
## Overview

This PR implements a smart contract system for tokenized commercial lighting maintenance using Clarity. The system consists of four main contracts that work together to manage commercial lighting facilities, fixtures, maintenance schedules, and energy tracking.

## Contracts

### 1. Facility Registration Contract
- Records details of illuminated properties
- Manages facility ownership and status
- Provides functions to register, update, and query facilities

### 2. Fixture Inventory Contract
- Tracks types and locations of lighting fixtures
- Links fixtures to facilities
- Provides functions to add, update, and query fixtures

### 3. Maintenance Scheduling Contract
- Manages bulb replacement timing
- Tracks maintenance history
- Provides functions to schedule and complete maintenance tasks

### 4. Energy Tracking Contract
- Monitors energy consumption
- Identifies potential savings
- Provides functions to record and analyze energy usage

## Testing

Tests are implemented using Vitest without relying on external libraries like @hirosystems/clarinet-sdk, @hirosystems/clarinet, @stacks/transactions, or @stacks/clarity. The tests use mock implementations to simulate the Clarity runtime environment.

## Implementation Details

- All contracts use simple data structures and functions
- Ownership and access control are implemented where appropriate
- The system is designed to be modular and extensible
- Error handling is implemented for common failure cases

## Future Improvements

- Implement token-based access control
- Add more sophisticated energy savings calculations
- Implement notifications for scheduled maintenance
- Add integration with IoT devices for automated readings

author: symbiomatrix
body:
Various trainers use different naming conventions for loras, which break the resize script. A ubiquitous one is lora_A / lora_B instead of lora_down / lora_up. This change reads whichever convention was used in the given model and adjusts all hardcoded references to that name.
A bit of a patchwork fix using global variables since I don't know the full flow of the code, but I've tested it extensively over several types of base models' loras (from 1.5 to wan) and it works for every lora I've tested.

This change removes the GitHub Actions workflow responsible for linting pull request titles and introduces a new configuration file, .github/semantic.yml, for semantic PR title validation. The new configuration enables status checks, restricts validation to PR titles only, and specifies a set of allowed scopes for PR titles. - Introduced a new configuration to enforce consistent semantic PR titles with restricted scope values.
