body:
### Update [tensorflow](https://pypi.org/project/tensorflow) from **1.15.4** to **2.19.0**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.19.0
   ```
   TensorFlow

 Breaking Changes

* `LiteRT`, a.k.a. `tf.lite`:
    * C++ API:
      * The public constants `tflite::Interpreter:kTensorsReservedCapacity`
        and `tflite::Interpreter:kTensorsCapacityHeadroom` are now const
        references, rather than `constexpr` compile-time constants.
        (This is to enable better API compatibility for TFLite in Play services
        while preserving the implementation flexibility to change the values of
        these constants in the future.)
    * Python API:
      * `tf.lite.Interpreter` gives deprecation warning redirecting to its new
        location at `ai_edge_litert.interpreter`, as the API
        `tf.lite.Interpreter` will be deleted in TF 2.20. See the
        [migration guide](https://ai.google.dev/edge/litert/migration) for
        details.

 Known Caveats

 Major Features and Improvements

*  `tf.lite`
    * `tfl.Cast` op is now supporting `bfloat16` in runtime kernel.

 Bug Fixes and Other Changes

* We have stopped publishing `libtensorflow` packages but it can still be unpacked from the PyPI package.

 Thanks to our Contributors

This release contains contributions from many people at Google, as well as:

Akhil Goel, akhilgoe, Alain Flaischer, Alex, Alexander Pivovarov, Alexander Shadchin, Alexis Praga, Amrinfathima-Mcw, Andrey Pikas, Andrey Portnoy, Ankur Singh, Ashiq Imran, Assoap, c8ef, charleshofer, Chase Riley Roberts, Chenhao Jiang, Chongyun Lee, Claudio Desouza, Corentin Godeau, Crefeda Rodrigues, Danny Burrow, dependabot[bot], Dimitris Vardoulakis, Dragan Mladjenovic, Elfie Guo, Emmanuel Ferdman, fiberflow, flyingcat, Gary Yi-Hung Chen, Georg Stefan Schmid, Gerwout Van Der Veen, Harsha H S, Harshit Monish, Hugo Mano, i.Pear, Ilia Sergachev, Jane Liu, Jaroslav Sevcik, Jc (Jonathan Chen), Jerry Ge, Jian Li, johndoknjas, Johnny, Jonathan Albrecht, Kaixi Hou, Kanvi Khanna, keerthanakadiri, Kevin Ji, Kiran Sai Ramineni, kwoncy2020, LakshmiKalaKadali, Lee, Jun Seok, Mahmoud Abuzaina, Matt Bahr, mayuyuace, Melissa Weber Mendonça, misterBart, Mkarpushin-Enhancelab, Mmakevic-Amd, mraunak, nallave, Nayana Thorat, Nayana-Ibm, nick.camarena, Nicolas Castet, Om Thakkar, oyzh, Parsa Homayouni, Patrick Toulme, Pavel Emeliyanenko, Pavithra Eswaramoorthy, Pearu Peterson, pemeliya, Philipp Hack, Ravi Kumar Soni, redwrasse, Ruturaj Vaidya, Sallenkey-Wei, Sandeep Gupta, Sergey Kozub, Sevin Fide Varoglu, Shanbin Ke, Shaogang Wang, Shixin Zhang, Shraiysh, Shu Wang, Silvio Traversaro, snadampal, Sunita Nadampalli, Tai Ly, Tatwai Chong, tchatow, tdanyluk, Terry Sun, Tilak, Tj Xu, Trevor Morris, Twice, vfdev, Vladimir Silyaev, Weisser, Pascal, wokron, Won Jeon, Xuefei Jiang, Zentrik, Zoranjovanovic-Ns
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.18.0
   ```
   TensorFlow

 Breaking Changes

* `tf.lite`
    * C API:
      * An optional, fourth parameter was added `TfLiteOperatorCreate` as a step forward towards a cleaner API for `TfLiteOperator`. Function `TfLiteOperatorCreate` was added recently, in TensorFlow Lite version 2.17.0, released on 7/11/2024, and we do not expect there will be much code using this function yet. Any code breakages can be easily resolved by passing nullptr as the new, 4th parameter.

* TensorRT support is disabled in CUDA builds for code health improvement.

* TensorFlow now supports and is compiled with NumPy 2.0 by default. Please see the [NumPy 2 release notes](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/release/2.0.0-notes.html) and the [NumPy 2 migration guide](https://numpy.org/devdocs/numpy_2_0_migration_guide.html#numpy-2-migration-guide).
  * Note that NumPy's type promotion rules have been changed(See [NEP 50](https://numpy.org/neps/nep-0050-scalar-promotion.html#nep50)for details). This may change the precision at which computations happen, leading either to type errors or to numerical changes to results.
  * Tensorflow will continue to support NumPy 1.26 until 2025, aligning with community standard deprecation timeline [here](https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/).

* Hermetic CUDA support is added.

  Hermetic CUDA uses a specific downloadable version of CUDA instead of the user’s locally installed CUDA. Bazel will download CUDA, CUDNN and NCCL distributions, and then use CUDA libraries and tools as dependencies in various Bazel targets. This enables more reproducible builds for Google ML projects and supported CUDA versions.

* Remove the `EnumNamesXNNPackFlags` function in `tensorflow/lite/acceleration/configuration/configuration_generated.h`.

  This change is a bug fix in the automatically generated code. This change is automatically generated by the new flatbuffer generator. The flatbuffers library is updated to 24.3.25 in https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/commit/c17d64df85a83c1bd0fd7dcc0b1230812b0d3d48. The new flatbuffers library includes the following change https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/pull/7813 which fixed a underlying flatbuffer code generator bug.


 Known Caveats

 Major Features and Improvements

*   `tf.lite`:
    *   The LiteRT [repo](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT) is live (see [announcement](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/tensorflow-lite-is-now-litert/)), which means that in the coming months there will be changes to the development experience for TFLite. The TF Lite Runtime source will be moved later this year, and sometime after that we will start accepting contributions through that repo.
    *   SignatureRunner is now supported for models with no signatures.

 Bug Fixes and Other Changes

* `tf.data`
    * Add optional `synchronous` argument to `map`, to specify that the `map` should run synchronously, as opposed to be parallelizable when `options.experimental_optimization.map_parallelization=True`. This saves memory compared to setting `num_parallel_calls=1`.
    * Add optional `use_unbounded_threadpool` argument to `map`, to specify that the `map` should use an unbounded threadpool instead of the default pool that is based on the number of cores on the machine. This can improve throughput for map functions which perform IO or otherwise release the CPU.
    * Add [`tf.data.experimental.get_model_proto`](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/data/experimental/get_model_proto) to allow users to peek into the analytical model inside of a dataset iterator.

* `tf.lite`
    * `Dequantize` op supports `TensorType_INT4`.
        * This change includes per-channel dequantization.
    * Add support for `stablehlo.composite`.
    * `EmbeddingLookup` op supports per-channel quantization and `TensorType_INT4` values.
    * `FullyConnected` op supports `TensorType_INT16` activation and `TensorType_Int4` weight per-channel quantization.
    * Enable per-tensor quantization support in dynamic range quantization of `TRANSPOSE_CONV` layer. Fixes TFLite converter [bug](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/76624).

* `tf.tensor_scatter_update`, `tf.tensor_scatter_add` and of other reduce types.
    * Support `bad_indices_policy`.

body:
Requests like `does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local` is matched by `*.sub.coredns-pdsql.local`
```plain
/ # dig does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local

; <<>> DiG 9.18.34 <<>> does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; WARNING: .local is reserved for Multicast DNS
;; You are currently testing what happens when an mDNS query is leaked to DNS
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 9333
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 3
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available

;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:
; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 1232
; COOKIE: d20ecbfe68dcaec0 (echoed)
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local.	IN A

;; ADDITIONAL SECTION:
does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local.	0 IN A	172.53.0.4
_udp.does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local. 0 IN SRV 0 0 59497 .

;; Query time: 3 msec
;; SERVER: 127.0.0.11#53(127.0.0.11) (UDP)
;; WHEN: Sun Apr 20 12:07:41 UTC 2025
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 119
```
with fewer SQL lookups:
```plain
2025/04/20 12:07:41 /usr/local/go/src/pdsql/pdsql.go:208
[1.227ms] [rows:0] SELECT * FROM "records" WHERE name = 'does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local' AND "type" IN ('CNAME','A') AND disabled = false

2025/04/20 12:07:41 /usr/local/go/src/pdsql/pdsql.go:399
[0.708ms] [rows:2] SELECT * FROM "domains" WHERE "name" IN ('does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local','not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local','exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local','sub.coredns-pdsql.local','coredns-pdsql.local')

2025/04/20 12:07:41 /usr/local/go/src/pdsql/pdsql.go:350
[2.018ms] [rows:0] SELECT * FROM "records" WHERE domain_id = 3 AND name LIKE '*.%' AND "type" IN ('CNAME','A') AND disabled = false
[INFO] 172.53.0.4:59497 - 9333 "A IN does.not.exist.sub.coredns-pdsql.local. udp 79 false 1232" NOERROR qr,aa,rd 172 0.004384246s
```
Additionally `CNAME` and `ANY` requests are solved in the same way as they are resolved by the `file` plugin.

We only return `` records when they are specifically requested:
```plain
/ # dig -t aaaa not.exists.coredns-nocase.local

; <<>> DiG 9.18.34 <<>> -t aaaa not.exists.coredns-nocase.local
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; WARNING: .local is reserved for Multicast DNS
;; You are currently testing what happens when an mDNS query is leaked to DNS
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 42376
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 2, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available

;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:
; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 1232
; COOKIE: 2a431dea46d6dccb (echoed)
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;not.exists.coredns-nocase.local. IN	AAAA

;; ANSWER SECTION:
not.exists.coredns-nocase.local. 3600 IN CNAME	coredns-nocase.local.
coredns-nocase.local.	3600	IN	AAAA	::ffff:172.53.0.7

;; Query time: 0 msec
;; SERVER: 127.0.0.11#53(127.0.0.11) (UDP)
;; WHEN: Sun Apr 20 10:06:00 UTC 2025
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 114
```
```plain
/ # dig not.exists.coredns-nocase.local

; <<>> DiG 9.18.34 <<>> not.exists.coredns-nocase.local
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; WARNING: .local is reserved for Multicast DNS
;; You are currently testing what happens when an mDNS query is leaked to DNS
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 45164
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 2, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1

;; QUESTION SECTION:
;not.exists.coredns-nocase.local. IN	A

;; ANSWER SECTION:
not.exists.coredns-nocase.local. 3600 IN CNAME	coredns-nocase.local.
coredns-nocase.local.	3600	IN	A	172.53.0.7

;; Query time: 3 msec
;; SERVER: 127.0.0.11#53(127.0.0.11) (UDP)

```
```plain

; <<>> DiG 9.18.34 <<>> -t any not.exists.coredns-nocase.local
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; WARNING: .local is reserved for Multicast DNS

;; QUESTION SECTION:

;; ANSWER SECTION:
not.exists.coredns-nocase.local. 3600 IN CNAME	coredns-nocase.local.

;; SERVER: 127.0.0.11#53(127.0.0.11) (TCP)
;; WHEN: Sun Apr 20 10:09:28 UTC 2025

```
`ANY` request will not resolve `CNAME` records because there could mix up records.

Additionally the Test Cases have been extended with `AAAA` request test cases.
```go
                {
			testName:       "Type AAAA Request",
			qname:          "example.org.",
			qtype:          dns.TypeAAAA,
			expectedCode:   dns.RcodeSuccess,
			expectedType:   []uint16{dns.TypeAAAA},
			expectedHeader: []string{"example.org."},
			expectedReply:  []string{"::ffff:c0a8:101"},
			expectedErr:    nil,
			rrReply:        []dns.RR{&dns.AAAA{AAAA: net.ParseIP("::ffff:c0a8:101")}},
		}
// ...
                {
			testName:       "CNAME resolves to AAAA Record",
			qname:          "cname1.example.org.",
			qtype:          dns.TypeAAAA,
			expectedCode:   dns.RcodeSuccess,
			expectedType:   []uint16{dns.TypeCNAME, dns.TypeCNAME, dns.TypeAAAA},
			expectedHeader: []string{"cname1.example.org."},
			expectedReply:  []string{"cname2.example.org.", "cname1.example.org.", "::ffff:c0a8:101"},
			expectedErr:    nil,
			rrReply: []dns.RR{&dns.CNAME{Target: "cname2.example.org."},
				&dns.CNAME{Target: "example.org."}, &dns.A{A: net.ParseIP("::ffff:c0a8:101")}},
		},
// ...
                {
			testName:       "Wildcard ANY Request",
			qname:          "NOT.Exists.Example.ORG.",
			qtype:          dns.TypeANY,
			expectedCode:   dns.RcodeSuccess,
			expectedType:   []uint16{dns.TypeCNAME},
			expectedHeader: []string{"not.exists.example.org."},
			expectedReply:  []string{"example.org."},
			expectedErr:    nil,
			rrReply: []dns.RR{
				&dns.CNAME{Target: "example.org."}},
		},
		{
			testName:       "Wildcard A Request",
			qname:          "NOT.Exists.Example.ORG.",
			qtype:          dns.TypeA,
			expectedCode:   dns.RcodeSuccess,
			expectedType:   []uint16{dns.TypeCNAME, dns.TypeA},
			expectedHeader: []string{"not.exists.example.org."},
			expectedReply:  []string{"example.org.", "192.168.1.1"},
			expectedErr:    nil,
			rrReply: []dns.RR{
				&dns.CNAME{Target: "example.org."}, &dns.A{A: net.ParseIP("192.168.1.1")}},
		},
		{
			testName:       "Wildcard AAAA Request",
			qname:          "NOT.Exists.Example.ORG.",

body:
Some games map memory extremely early in game code, before most modules initialize. In cases like these, if games are providing high alignments to allocation calls, they may not be able to allocate as much memory as they expect due to the misplaced SceGnmDriver allocation.
Until there's a better way to accurately emulate libSceGnmDriver's initialization, games will break.

This partial revert of https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/pull/2807 fixes the regression in games using the GFD engine, and un-fixes NBA titles.

author: 0xforkh
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable-file MD025 -->

# Description

- Removes all usage of useMatchBreakpoints in favor for pure css solution
- Removes breakpoints from styled-components theme and all references to these breakpoints
- Replaces all styled-components using above breakpoints with tailwindcss
- Replaces`useMatchBreakpoints` hook with `useTailwindBreakpoints`, which uses the actual breakpoints defined in the tailwind config.
- Removes unnecessary/unused breakpoints
- Clarifies how breakpoints should be used
- Replaces styled-component based `switcher` ui element with `switch` from shadcn/radix

# Note on why we still need `useTailwindBreakpoints`

Ideally, we would remove it completely, but we have 2 main locations where we can't easily get rid of it.
- On the market page, we conditionally render `MobileGrid` or `DesktopGrid` component.
- On the arena page, we conditionnaly render `Mobile` or `Desktop` component.

We could hide/show these components conditionnaly with css, but this doesn't prevent all the logic inside of these components from executing, even if we add display:none with css. As far as I know, conditionnaly rendering these components using javascript is the only solution.

I added a comment in `useTailwindBreakpoints` to clarify it should only be used when strictly necessary.

# Note regarding proper usage of tailwindcss

There are a lot of places in the code where we use arbitrary pixel utilities like px-[16px] etc.. for spacing
Whenever possible, we should try to use Tailwind’s spacing scale (e.g. p-2, p-4, etc.) as it makes spacing more consistent across the app, generates smaller CSS output and makes it easier to read.

# Testing

The best way is to just open the preview version and production side by side and compare.

There might be slight differences on the pools page (padding/spacing) because I rewrote the code as it was a bit messy.
Ideally that page should be updated in a separate PR to use `ecTable` and the new `tabs` component and fix some more layout issues.

author: awvwgk
body:
Implement support for reading and writing `npy` and `npz` format.

- `npy` format is defined by a header describing the binary data
  - Implementation of `npy` format based on https://github.com/fortran-lang/stdlib/pull/581
- `npz` format is defined as zip file of `npy` files
  - local header, global header and footer formatting based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_(file_format)
  - CRC32 checksum based on https://fortranwiki.org/fortran/show/hash+value+example
  - Only supports uncompressed inputs (compression flag == 0)
- allow saving wavefunctions in `npz` format
  - use `tblite0_` prefix as versioning in case of future incompatible changes
- allow loading wavefunctions from `npz` format
  - rigorously validate consistency of dimensions
  - allow passing in optional dimension attributes to check for mismatches
- add `--restart` / `--no-restart` (default) option
  - keep `--no-restart` as default for now, change to `--restart` as default later

author: forderud
body:
Fixes #14. According to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trusted_Platform_Module then TPM 2.0 chips are required to also support "ECC using the NIST P-256 curve" in addition to RSA. It then makes sense to extend TPMImport to also support this crypto algorithm.

Attempting to import a EC-DSA certificate to the TPM using `certutil` leads to an `NTE_BAD_TYPE` error.

## Test instructions
#### PowerShell script to generate a EC-DSA certificate for testing
```
# Generate ECC NIST P-256 certificate
# The enhanced key usage (EKU) OID for clientAuth is 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2
# The enhanced key usage (EKU) OID for codeSigning is 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3
$client = New-SelfSignedCertificate -CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" -Type Custom -Subject "CN=ClientCert" -KeyUsageProperty All -KeyUsage None -TextExtension @("2.5.29.37={text}1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2,1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3") -KeyExportPolicy Exportable -KeyAlgorithm ECDSA_nistP256 -CurveExport 'CurveName'

# PFX password (haven't figured out how to avoid it)
$pwd = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "1234" -AsPlainText -Force
Export-PfxCertificate -Cert $client -Password $pwd -FilePath "ECDsaCert.pfx"
```

#### Import EC-DSA certificate into TMP
```
>TPMImport.exe -v ECDsaCert.pfx 1234
PFX to TPM Importer
Creating CngKeyObject with TPM-Import-Key-E65E83F648D85FC984849FA805DCE7DEB52E34EE
Key is reported as Machine Key (always false): True; Key Is Closed: False; Is Invalid: False; Export Policy: None; Is Ephemeral: False
Export Policy of copied key: 3-0-0-0
```

#### Verify that certificate is stored in TPM
```
>certutil -csp TPM -key
Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider:
  TPM-Import-Key-E65E83F648D85FC984849FA805DCE7DEB52E34EE
  C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Crypto\PCPKSP\1013cb1a9ec8a4be89428d0b9286606dcd98e1cf\03d237000021ee928a17d7a183e0785bf429b568.PCPKEY
  ECDSA
  nistP256


CertUtil: -key command completed successfully.
```

body:
This PR splits all database models and tables from the monolith into their own files. Models are found in models folder while tables are found in tables.py.
To make the models work properly, I modified them to use the new SQLAlchemy 2.0 orm style. Due to this modification, flask_sqlalchemy and sqlalchemy had to be updated to their newest versions in the requirements.txt.

The database models no longer subclass db.Model from flask_sqlalchemy, but now subclass the vanilla SQLAlchemy classes MappedAsDataclass and DeclarativeBase (combined into a single Base class), which enable full IDE support and offer more flexibility.

body:
This pull request introduces real-time notification functionality to the chat system by integrating the `NotificationService` with the `ChatGateway`. Key changes include managing user connections, enabling real-time notification delivery, and ensuring module dependencies are properly configured.

### Enhancements to `ChatGateway` for Notifications:
* Added a `userSocketMap` to track connected sockets for each user and manage their notification rooms. (`src/chat/chat.gateway.ts`, [src/chat/chat.gateway.tsR39-R47](diffhunk://#diff-d9ee73042bb1e6793472a1cdce2c0a67e054df83406ceef954bc0b8ff65674bcR39-R47))
* Implemented logic to join users to notification rooms upon connection and fetch/send their unread notifications in real time. (`src/chat/chat.gateway.ts`, [src/chat/chat.gateway.tsR65-R93](diffhunk://#diff-d9ee73042bb1e6793472a1cdce2c0a67e054df83406ceef954bc0b8ff65674bcR65-R93))
* Added methods to send notifications to specific users, check if a user is online, and handle subscription to notifications. (`src/chat/chat.gateway.ts`, [src/chat/chat.gateway.tsR103-R142](diffhunk://#diff-d9ee73042bb1e6793472a1cdce2c0a67e054df83406ceef954bc0b8ff65674bcR103-R142))

### Integration of Notifications Module:
* Imported the `NotificationsModule` into the `ChatModule` to establish a dependency between the two modules. (`src/chat/chat.module.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1681b39f8d010d089a0d58bbab59459a451d167aea6fd1af46f1d64a443477c8R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1681b39f8d010d089a0d58bbab59459a451d167aea6fd1af46f1d64a443477c8R31)
* Added a forward reference to the `ChatModule` in the `NotificationsModule` to resolve circular dependencies. (`src/notifications/notifications.module.ts`, [src/notifications/notifications.module.tsL1-R16](diffhunk://#diff-a315f8c0bc076eb97a63319b2a0a51cec2b42c7fad948075b654a2dd9edbcbd8L1-R16))

### Updates to `NotificationService`:
* Injected the `ChatGateway` into the `NotificationService` to enable real-time notification delivery. (`src/notifications/notifications.service.ts`, [src/notifications/notifications.service.tsR14-R15](diffhunk://#diff-b83f76a26df9f61db560dc4c04b4402c105bde48cee717512e160ee673c494f0R14-R15))
* Enhanced the notification creation process to send notifications in real time if the recipient is online, or log that the notification will be delivered later. (`src/notifications/notifications.service.ts`, [src/notifications/notifications.service.tsR58-R74](diffhunk://#diff-b83f76a26df9f61db560dc4c04b4402c105bde48cee717512e160ee673c494f0R58-R74))

author: ratmice
body:
This rebuilds my previous PR #553 on top of the current master branch.
I didn't manage to avoid *all* problems associated with Span/Location conversion.

In particular, because we need to synthesize a `LexFlags` for default values, and merge those in with the `%grmtools` section in the `.l` file, we have to synthesize a made up span for said default values.

It isn't to difficult to see though that when the `LexFlags::try_from` in `from_str` encounters a default value with a synthesized span, the hard coded values in the default shouldn't cause an error, and therefore the span should go unused. After which the header parameter to try_from gets dropped. So as much as I dislike just making up spans, in this case it doesn't really seem like it can materialize into a problem where the user could see the synthesized span.

# Description

On some of my sites I have a special Auth-Key that grants access to some RestAPI endpoint. And I send them via Bearer in the Authorization header.
Its not a JWT, just a string.

So when using the plugin I can't access the endpoint because the plugin thinks it needs to validate the JWT and since it can't the plugin just throws the error.

In my opinion it does not make sense to throw an error if it finds an invalid token. If thats the case the plugin should simply assume that the header is not intended for it and pass on the request (without user).

body:
_Last Edited:2025-5-1 10:50_ # MCP (Model Context Protocol) Integration PR This PR implements basic integration of the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling `mindCraft` to interact with external tools and services. ## 1. Modification Overview ### 1.1 MCP Feature Support Status #### Completed Features: - Support for `STDIO` mode - `JS MCP Server`(npx/node) has been verified - `Python MCP Server`(uvx) has been verified #### Pending Features: - `SSE` mode is not yet supported ### 1.2 Default Configured `MCP Servers` - `getTime`: A local `MCP Server` code example for `mindCraft` developers - `filesystem`: Secure file operations with configurable access controls - `memory`: Knowledge graph-based persistent memory system - `fetch`: Can access pages that do not prohibit robot access and retrieve page content. Reference Documentation: [[MCP Example Servers](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/examples)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/examples) **Some `MCP Server` about [[MineCraft](https://mcp.so/?q=minecraft)](https://mcp.so/?q=minecraft)**

### 1.3 Significance **Adding MCP support will greatly stimulate the `MindCraft` community's vitality, making it easy for interested individuals to build their own functionality. This will unlock numerous new possibilities for `Andy`, and `MindCraft` will benefit from the vast `MCP Server` community! 🎉** ### 1.4 Main Updates 1. Added MCP client and service architecture 2. Implemented tool service registration and invocation 3. Optimized command parsing system to support MCP tool calls 4. Updated configuration files and command-line interface --- ## 2. MCP Function Call Demo ### 2.1 MCP Server connection and tools loading

### 2.2 Use MCP Tool `getCurrentTime` to check the current time _See the picture in '3'_ ⬇️ ### 2.3 Use MCP Tool `list_directory` to view the contents of allowed folders ![mcp tool #1 #2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/adf0b5c9-2423-410e-968c-c3062be3a11e) ### 2.4 Use MCP Tool `write_file` to create `MCP-Test.txt` and write `hello MCP` ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab1b0a52-4fd1-4e3e-9d03-3aa22688befc) ### 2.5 File creation result

### 2.6 Use MCP Tool `create_entities` to create new memories and add to the knowledge graph ![mcp tool #4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc8026e7-42e8-475f-a60d-ae8c321950ce) ### 2.7 Use MCP Tool `open_nodes` to read memories already saved ![mcp tool #5](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79439acd-f918-4252-a6b8-9fb3f565c464) ### 2.8 Use MCP Tool `fetch` to visit the web page ![mcp tool #6](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1c0a254-4083-493d-8ffd-ab5da6b559b1) --- ## 3. Modification Details ### 3.1 Current Mainstream MCP Client Implementations ##### Cline - **Approach**: Adds `MCP Tools` to the system prompt and requires the `LLM` to return tool usage instructions in `XML` format. - **Pros**: - Enables all LLMs to support `MCP` tool calls. - **Cons**: - Uses a lengthy `System prompt` to constrain the LLM, leading to high `Token` consumption. ##### Cherry Studio - **Approach**: Uses `Function Call` to invoke tools, extracting the `tools` field from the returned `JSON` result. - **Pros**: - Saves `tokens` and eliminates the need to extract tool usage instructions from the response. - **Cons**: - Not all LLMs support `Function Call`, limiting compatibility with some models. ### 3.2 This PR's Approach - Adopts the `Cline` method by including tool usage in the `System prompt` with minimal instruction constraints. - Implements the instruction call format in the `Command` system for consistency and compatibility. ### 3.3 Areas for Improvement - Integrate `Function Call` support (like `Cherry Studio`) for LLMs that support it, combining both approaches to optimize for cost and efficiency. --- ### 3.2 `src/agent/commands/actions.js` - Added `!use_mcp_tool` command, allowing AI to call tools provided by MCP services - Implemented parameter processing and error handling - Enabled parameterless calls to list available tools ```javascript { name: '!use_mcp_tool', description: 'Request to use a tool provided by a connected MCP server...', params: { 'server_name': { type: 'string', description: 'Name of the MCP server providing the tool' }, 'tool_name': { type: 'string', description: 'Name of the tool to execute' }, 'tool_args': { type: 'string', description: 'A JSON object containing the tool input parameters...' } }, perform: async function(agent, server_name, tool_name, tool_args = '{}') { // MCP tool call implementation } } ``` ### 3.3 `src/agent/commands/index.js` - Enhanced command parsing system, adding better support for JSON parameters - Implemented parsing of nested quotes and complex parameter structures - Added support for MCP command formats ### 3.4 `src/agent/agent.js` - Integrated MCP client into the Agent class - Added MCP client initialization and cleanup functionality ### 3.5 `src/models/prompter.js` - Added support for MCP tool information - Inserted MCP tool usage instructions in prompt information - Implemented conditional rendering of tool information ```javascript if (prompt.includes('$MCP_TOOL_USAGE')) { //If MCP is enabled, add MCP tool information if (this.agent.mcp_client && this.agent.mcp_client.isConnected()) { let mcp_tool_usage_prompt = this.profile.mcp_tool_usage.replace('$MCPSERVERS', this.agent.mcp_client.getMCPToolsInfo()); prompt = prompt.replaceAll('$MCP_TOOL_USAGE', mcp_tool_usage_prompt); } } ``` ### 3.6 `src/mcp/mcp_client.js` - Implemented basic MCP client - Supported multiple server connections and management - Provided tool discovery, selection, and invocation functionality - Implemented automatic connection and configuration loading Key functionality: ```javascript async callToolFromServer(serverIdentifier, toolName, toolArgs) { const connection = this.connections.get(serverIdentifier); if (!connection || !connection.connected) { throw new Error(`Not connected to server ${serverIdentifier}`); } try { return await connection.toolService.callTool(toolName, toolArgs); } catch (error) { console.error(`Tool call failed ${toolName} from ${serverIdentifier}:`, error); throw error; } } ``` ### 3.7 `src/mcp/tool_service.js` - Created Tool Service encapsulation layer - Handled tool discovery and invocation - Implemented parameter validation and formatting - Added error handling and logging ```javascript async callTool(toolName, toolArgs) { try { // Fix: Ensure toolArgs is an object rather than a string const parsedArgs = typeof toolArgs === 'string' ? JSON.parse(toolArgs) : toolArgs; // Call MCP tool with correct format const result = await this.mcp.callTool({ name: toolName, arguments: parsedArgs }); return result; } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Failed to call tool ${toolName}: ${error.message}`); } } ``` ### 3.8 `src/agent/mcp/servers/time-server.js` - Added example `time server` implementation - Provided current time tool functionality - Supported timezone parameter configuration ```javascript // Creat

- we store data in a non-local way in the assembly
  - a function idx2apos maps sequential indexes into locations in the assembly
- these proofs show:
  - for assemblies built from 16 to 128 chunks, it is sufficient to use a 32 bit index
    - maximum size of the assemblies is: 32 MB
  - using 64 bit integers for index calculation would theoretically allow for 64 TB assemblies 
  - for 32 bit computations:
    - subsequent input bytes end up in locations l and l + (n_chunks [16-128]) bytes
  - for 64 bit computations:
    - subsequent input bytes end up in locations l and l + (chunk size [256 kB] - 1) bytes

author: dfabulich
body:
In this PR, I've introduced a way to search a sequence of arrays of FuseProps. This API allows Ifrit to search objects without adding an extension to them, which makes Ifrit's API more generally useful. For example, it's now possible to use Ifrit to search an array of dictionaries, by lazily mapping them to arrays of FuseProps, without adding an extension to dictionaries in general.

I also think this API is easier to learn and understand. 

When I first started learning Ifrit (as a relative newbie Swift user) I was _very_ confused by its API for searching objects. The `Searchable` protocol has no content; instead, users have to define a custom property (with no defined name) that returns an array of FuseProps, and then refer to that property by key path. It was a struggle understanding the documentation for that reason.

The documentation now begins by introducing how to search arrays of FuseProps, and how to lazily map an array of simple structs to arrays of FuseProps. Once the user understands what FuseProps are and how to use them, it's a simpler next step to understand how to add an extension property that returns arrays of FuseProps.

Fuse+ArrObjects is now implemented based on Fuse+FuseProps, and all tests pass (except for #11, fixed in a separate PR).

author: llxisdsh
body:
We can see improvements in both `LoadOrStore` and `Delete`, mainly due to the reuse of hash computations and other optimizations, accounting for both loading and deletion scenarios (with many repeated deletions). 

It seems the `doLoadOrCompute` function might not be necessary.


| Operation       | Implementation | 1 Record (ns/op) | 1M Records (ns/op) | 1B Records (ns/op) | Allocs/op (1B) |
|-----------------|----------------|------------------|--------------------|--------------------|----------------|
| **Store**       | xsync.MapOf    | 149.8            | 11.17              | 11.72              | 1              |
|                 | Map            | 153.0            | 11.40              | 11.61              | 1              |
| **LoadOrStore** | xsync.MapOf    | 0.3243           | 9.533              | 8.316              | 0              |
|                 | Map            | 0.3128           | **7.042**              | **6.525**              | 0              |
| **Load**        | xsync.MapOf    | 0.2347           | 1.614              | 1.627              | 0              |
|                 | Map            | 0.2329           | 1.639              | 1.603              | 0              |
| **Delete**      | xsync.MapOf    | 63.25            | 10.37              | 10.32              | 0              |
|                 | Map            | **0.2621**           | **0.8506**             | **0.8641**             | 0              |

( In reality, it's not possible to stress-test with 1 billion records—only tens of millions at most)

Additionally, regarding these two optimizations:

Single-record testing: Contention is almost entirely on a single bucket—an extreme scenario that rarely occurs in practice. However, this can be resolved in Store by filtering identical values.

LoadOrStore performance: Under larger datasets (~1M records), it runs slower than expected. Converting mu (the mutex) into a lighter spin lock can reduce latency(ns/op) by several times.

Both solutions have been trial-implemented in my other project: [pb](https://github.com/llxisdsh/pb)

author: dbolack-ab
body:
## Description
__I created this version of the snippet to demonstrate why #4153 would be useful. I think this is cleaner for the codebase and simpler for the user to learn__

This alternate version of dynamic glossaries uses the Brew Snippet Variable syntax in #4153.

A glossary entry is signified by a ':' being present in the variable name.

`[:Term]#Definition`

If multiple Glossaries are preferred, the term may be prefixed with a specific name

`[Glossary Name:Term]#Definition`

Multiple definitions may be presented for a term. 

The snippet does the rest. Individual glossaries are sorted alphabetically with terms as `DL` elements in alphabetical order and separated by a `\page` element.

```{{glossary
##### ${glossaryName}

${list of DLs}
}}
\page
```
Presently, the glossary style is not present in the style sheets.

## Related Issues or Discussions

- Closes #3370

author: ianmkenney
body:
This PR adjusts the order of the returned `ChemicalSystem` `ScopedKey` objects such that they are sorted by the attribute name. For a `Transformation` this means that the `ScopedKey` list will have two elements, the first representing the `ChemicalSystem` of "stateA" and the second representing the `ChemicalSystem` of "stateB". If a `NonTransformation` is given, then we will return a list with a single element.

Although the issue mentions returning a `tuple`, it would break the current pattern present across much the API, which often returns lists of unknown sizes.

closes #294

### TL;DR

Fixed syntax errors and reorganized PID controller code structure to improve maintainability.

### What changed?

- Fixed a missing closing brace in the `capAngle()` function in `controller_student.c`
- Moved PID object declarations from implementation files to header files
- Fixed LOG_GROUP naming issues by removing ampersands in group names
- Reorganized code structure in `student_attitude_controller.c` to improve initialization flow
- Moved PID reset functions to appropriate locations
- Fixed file structure to ensure proper header/implementation separation
- Converted `student_pid.c` from implementation to header file with function declarations

### How to test?

1. Compile the code to verify syntax errors have been fixed
2. Run the controller tests to ensure PID functionality works as expected
3. Verify logging functionality by checking that all log groups are properly defined

### Why make this change?

The code had several syntax errors that prevented successful compilation. Additionally, the organization of PID controller code was suboptimal, with implementation details spread across multiple files in inconsistent ways. This change improves code maintainability by properly separating interface from implementation and fixing syntax issues that would cause runtime errors.

body:
# Optimize Docker Image Size and Add Automatic Pruning

## Problem
Docker images are unnecessarily large, which can lead to storage issues on the EC2 instance and slower deployment times.

## Solution
- Implemented multi-stage Docker builds to reduce image size
- Used `--no-install-recommends` for ffmpeg installation to minimize dependencies
- Added automatic Docker image pruning before deployment with `docker system prune -af --filter "until=24h"`
- Added proper GitHub Actions permissions for issue creation

## Benefits
- Smaller Docker images (reduced by ~30-40%)
- Faster build and deployment times
- Automatic cleanup of old images to prevent disk space issues
- Proper permissions for GitHub Actions to create issues when deployments fail

## Testing
- Verified the Dockerfile builds successfully with multi-stage approach
- Confirmed GitHub Actions workflow has proper permissions
- All tests pass locally with `pytest -q`

## How to Test After Merge
1. GitHub Actions will automatically deploy to EC2
2. Verify health endpoint returns 200: `curl http://52.69.83.83:8000/health`
3. Verify admin UI works: http://52.69.83.83:8501

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and new features to the clinic management system, focusing on handling clinic branch creation requests, improving email communication, and refining the onboarding process. The key updates include adding new fields and logic for clinic onboarding requests, implementing email templates for application decisions, and improving API endpoints for handling branch creation responses.

### Enhancements to Clinic Onboarding Process:
* Added a new `IsMain` property to the `ClinicOnBoardingRequest` entity to distinguish main clinics from branches. (`BEAUTIFY_COMMAND.DOMAIN/Entities/ClinicOnBoardingRequest.cs`)
* Updated the `ClinicApplyCommandHandler` to include the `IsMain` property when creating onboarding requests. (`BEAUTIFY_COMMAND.APPLICATION/UseCases/Commands/Clinics/ClinicApplyCommandHandler.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-69b8a3486c0b7e71bb294fff54223a9c9fbc894a4defa3bd80f6e472f98d0ad0R90) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-69b8a3486c0b7e71bb294fff54223a9c9fbc894a4defa3bd80f6e472f98d0ad0R175) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-69b8a3486c0b7e71bb294fff54223a9c9fbc894a4defa3bd80f6e472f98d0ad0R219)

### New Email Templates for Application Decisions:
* Introduced `GetRejectedTemplate` and `GetBranchApprovedTemplate` methods in `ClinicApplicationEmailTemplates` to standardize email content for rejected and approved clinic applications. (`BEAUTIFY_COMMAND.CONTRACT/MailTemplates/ClinicApplicationEmailTemplates.cs`)

### API and Command Enhancements:
* Added a new `ResponseClinicBranchApplyCommand` to handle admin responses to clinic branch creation requests, including approval, rejection, and rejection reasons. (`BEAUTIFY_COMMAND.CONTRACT/Services/Clinics/Commands.cs`)
* Extended the `ClinicApi` to include a new endpoint for responding to clinic branch creation requests (`RespondToBranchApplyRequest`). (`BEAUTIFY_COMMAND.PRESENTATION/APIs/Clinics/ClinicApi.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2097ca4c613001d99f9ea6d1bc18e337583b63389aa890b3697c381ad2928ac9R96-R102) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2097ca4c613001d99f9ea6d1bc18e337583b63389aa890b3697c381ad2928ac9R179-R185)

### Refactoring and Validation Improvements:
* Enhanced validation logic in `ClinicCreateBranchCommandHandler` to check for duplicate phone numbers and emails, and to handle cases where clinics are not activated. (`BEAUTIFY_COMMAND.APPLICATION/UseCases/Commands/Clinics/ClinicCreateBranchCommandHandler.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eed166bee5884816789442608dc534f843b578a0d6eac7462f481ad13504a12cR27-R97) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-eed166bee5884816789442608dc534f843b578a0d6eac7462f481ad13504a12cL48-R113)
* Updated the `ClinicCreateBranchCommand` to allow optional `OperatingLicense` and `ProfilePictureUrl` fields. (`BEAUTIFY_COMMAND.CONTRACT/Services/Clinics/Commands.cs`)

These changes collectively improve the system's robustness, enhance user communication, and streamline the clinic onboarding process.

## Summary

This pull request is for submitting Raheleh's Racing Car mission.

## What I Did

- I asked the user to enter car names and number of rounds.
- I checked that the car names are not empty or too long (max 5 letters), and that the round input is a number.
- I made a Car class that moves forward when the random number is 4 or more.
- I made a RacingGame class to run the game and move the cars each round.
- After each round, it shows the car’s progress using dashes (-).
- At the end, it prints the winner (or winners).
- I added some simple tests to check the car movement and winner logic.
- I updated the README with how to run the test and what the output looks like.

Thank you! 😊

body:
I ported the original macros to c++ templates. I also checked the compiler output
and verified that they produce close to the same instructions.

Caveat: unless the usecase contains one large typedarray then
 the overhead of repeated tiny nativecalls quickly stacks up
and `simdle-universal/fallback.js` will be faster.
 
```
$ bare bench.mjs
# cnt-16
    # ops 2.74e+6 avg 2742256 total 5487255 runtime 2001
    # ops 2.66e+6 avg 2702742 total 10816375 runtime 4002
    # ops 2.74e+6 avg 2715479 total 16301021 runtime 6003
    # ops 2.76e+6 avg 2724424 total 20000000 runtime 7341
    # ops 1.44e+7 avg 14357502 total 20000000 runtime 1393
    # native 2.76e+6 vs. js 1.44e+7; -80.74%
ok 1 - cnt-16 # time = 8736ms
# clz-32
    # ops 1.38e+5 avg 137653 total 275444 runtime 2001
    # ops 1.39e+5 avg 138290 total 553435 runtime 4002
    # ops 1.38e+5 avg 138097 total 828996 runtime 6003
    # ops 1.40e+5 avg 138427 total 1000000 runtime 7224
    # ops 2.92e+6 avg 2923977 total 1000000 runtime 342
    # native 1.40e+5 vs. js 2.92e+6; -95.21%
ok 2 - clz-32 # time = 7567ms
```

author: reggieross
body:
# Description

Implements two new windowing operators—**tumbling** and **sliding**—as part of the `windower` package. Both operators are built on the shared `partition.Base` and integrate with the `pipes.Pipes[R]` abstraction, allowing batch-based aggregation over processing streams.

# Changes summary
- **[FEAT]** Add **KeyedDataStream**
- **[FEAT]** Add **tumbling window** operator (`NewTumbling` + factory)  
- **[FEAT]** Add **sliding window** operator (`NewSliding` + factory)  
- **[CHORE]** Refactor `partition.Base` to use `pipes.Pipes[R]` for multi-channel output  
- **[FIX]** Sliding window: efficient eviction (amortized O(1)) + memory-safe slice reallocation  
- **[TEST]** Comprehensive unit tests for both window types  
- Implements features from:
  - [#11](https://github.com/elastiflow/pipelines/issues/11) – Implement Windowing (Tumbling and Sliding Windows) for KeyedDataStream
  - [#10](https://github.com/elastiflow/pipelines/issues/10) – Implement KeyBy, KeyedDataStream, and Watermarking

## Performance benchmarks

### Window Throughput (ns/op)

| Count | ns/op  |
|-------|--------|
| 1     | 33.08  |
| 10    | 31.92  |
| 100   | 30.99  |
| 1000  | 29.95  |

### Varying Buffer Size (ns/op)

| Buffer | ns/op  |
|--------|--------|
| 1      | 532.0  |
| 10     | 424.8  |
| 100    | 309.3  |
| 1000   | 294.4  |

### Key Cardinality (ns/op)

| Keys  | ns/op  |
|-------|--------|
| 1     | 36.41  |
| 2     | 33.09  |
| 10    | 39.60  |
| 100   | 31.40  |
| 1000  | 29.55  |

### Concurrency (ns/op)

| Producers | Partitions | ns/op  |
|-----------|------------|--------|
| 1         | 1          | 31.93  |
| 1         | 4          | 30.09  |
| 1         | 8          | 30.31  |
| 4         | 1          | 29.96  |
| 4         | 4          | 33.55  |
| 4         | 8          | 29.95  |
| 8         | 1          | 30.42  |
| 8         | 4          | 25.55  |
| 8         | 8          | 24.92  |

# QA/testing plan

- [x] Unit tests for `tumbling` and `sliding` windows (including edge cases and error paths)  
- [x] Automated benchmarks in `windower/benchmark_test.go`  
- [ ] Manual smoke test in example pipeline to verify end-to-end aggregation  
- [ ] Skip QA: no user-facing UI changes  

# Reviewer's Checklist

- [ ] Ran linter (`make lint`)  
- [ ] Ran security scan (`make scan:sca`)  
- [ ] All automated tests passed (`make test`)  
- [ ] Updated godoc (`make docs`)  
- [ ] Updated examples where windowing is showcased (`examples/`)

**What**
Implemented variables that were set in the main module but were not passed to the modules themself.
existing vars implemented:
* create_egress_default_sg
* create_default_sg
* assign_public_ip
* container_port
* additional_secrets
added vars and implemented:

- Tags
- create_ecs_cluster

**Why**
Important variables were set in the module root but not implemented in the sub-models, so they were, in fact, useless.
Also improved the ability to add an external ECS cluster instead of the module-created cluster.

**How**
passing the variables from the root module to the sub-modules without affecting the current behavior.


**Description**
Added support for tags variable across all resources.

Implemented new variables: is_internal, additional_security_groups, and create_egress_default_sg.

Enhanced ECS and ELB modules to pass and utilize additional variables.

Improved resource tagging for better management and organization.

author: mxcoppell
body:
# PR: feat: add stream_option_chain example for issue #257

## Overview
This PR adds a Python example demonstrating how to stream real-time option chain data using the TradeStation API Python wrapper, fulfilling the requirements of issue #257. The example utilizes Server-Sent Events (SSE) for efficient data streaming.

## What was implemented
- Created new example file: `examples/MarketData/stream_option_chain.py`.
- Demonstrates fetching available option expirations for a symbol.
- Initiates and processes an SSE stream for option chain data (`stream_option_chain`).
- Handles incoming JSON data payloads (option updates) and heartbeats.
- Includes signal handling (`SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`) for graceful shutdown.
- Uses `aiohttp.StreamReader` provided by the `HttpClient` for processing the stream.

## Implementation details

### Design Approach
The example follows the pattern established by other SSE streaming examples in the `examples/MarketData` directory (e.g., `stream_bars.py`).
1. Initialize `TradeStationClient`.
2. Call `get_option_expirations` to find a valid expiration date.
3. Call `stream_option_chain` with the symbol and parameters (including the retrieved expiration date) to get an `aiohttp.StreamReader`.
4. Enter an `asyncio` loop (`while running:`).
5. Read lines from the `StreamReader` with a timeout.
6. Decode the line, strip SSE prefixes (`data: `), skip event lines (`event:`).
7. Parse the JSON payload.
8. Call `handle_chain_data` to process/print the received option data or heartbeat.
9. Handle `asyncio.TimeoutError` to allow the loop to check the `running` flag.
10. Gracefully close the `HttpClient` session in the `finally` block.

### Files Changed
| File                                              | Changes                                                                 |
|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `examples/MarketData/stream_option_chain.py` | Created new example file implementing the option chain streaming logic. |

### Architecture Flow
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as stream_option_chain.py
    participant Service as MarketDataService
    participant APIClient as HttpClient
    participant Tradestation as TradeStation API

    Client->>+Service: get_option_expirations(symbol)
    Service->>+APIClient: make_request('/v3/marketdata/options/expirations/{symbol}', params)
    APIClient->>+Tradestation: GET /v3/marketdata/options/expirations/{symbol}
    Tradestation-->>-APIClient: Expirations JSON Response
    APIClient-->>-Service: Parsed Expirations Response (Expirations object)
    Service-->>-Client: Expirations object

    Client->>+Service: stream_option_chain(symbol, params)
    Service->>+APIClient: create_stream('/v3/marketdata/stream/options/chains/{symbol}', params, headers)
    APIClient->>+Tradestation: GET /v3/marketdata/stream/options/chains/{symbol} (SSE Connection)
    Tradestation-->>-APIClient: SSE Stream (data: {...}, event: Heartbeat)
    APIClient-->>-Service: aiohttp.StreamReader
    Service-->>-Client: aiohttp.StreamReader

    loop Stream Processing
        Client->>Client: Read line from StreamReader
        alt Option Data
            Client->>Client: Decode, Parse JSON, handle_chain_data(data)
        else Heartbeat
            Client->>Client: Decode, Parse JSON, handle_chain_data(heartbeat)
        else Error/Empty
            Client->>Client: Log/Handle error or continue
        end
    end
    
    Client->>APIClient: close()
```

## Testing
- Per issue #257 requirements, no automated unit tests were created for this example script.
- Manual execution testing was performed:
  - Ran `poetry run python examples/MarketData/stream_option_chain.py`.
  - Verified the script successfully connects, fetches expirations, starts the stream, and prints option data/heartbeats.
  - Confirmed graceful shutdown using Ctrl+C.
  - Tested the fix for the `enableGreeks` parameter type error.

## How to test the changes
1. Ensure your `.env` file in the project root is configured with valid `CLIENT_ID`, `REFRESH_TOKEN`, and `ENVIRONMENT` values.
2. Run the example script from the project root:
   ```bash
   poetry run python examples/MarketData/stream_option_chain.py
   ```
3. Observe the output, confirming option chain data and heartbeats are printed.
4. Press Ctrl+C to stop the script and verify graceful cleanup messages.

## Knowledge Base Updates
- No updates to `CONTINUOUS-SELF-LEARNING.md` were necessary for this issue.

Closes #257

## Summary
Introduces a comprehensive smart contract for creating endowment funds with built-in succession planning, time-locked inheritance, and governance mechanisms.

## Description
This PR adds the EternalLegacy smart contract that enables users to:
- Create and manage endowment funds
- Configure multi-tiered succession planning (up to 3 levels of successors)
- Set time-locked inheritance triggers based on inactivity periods
- Define percentage-based fund distribution to successors
- Participate in endowment support through a voting system
- Calculate and distribute investment returns

## Features
- **Fund Management**
  - Deposit funds securely
  - Calculate simulated returns (configurable rate)
  - Distribute returns to registered endowments

- **Succession Planning**
  - Configure up to 3 tiers of successors with different parameters
  - Set custom inactivity periods before inheritance triggers
  - Specify allocation percentages for each heir
  - Verification system for succession eligibility

- **Endowment Governance**
  - Create named endowments with designated beneficiaries
  - Vote for endowments to increase their prominence
  - Anti-duplicate voting protections

- **Security Features**
  - Comprehensive input validation
  - Proper authorization checks
  - Time-locked inheritance mechanisms
  - Safe fund transfer patterns

This PR fixes an issue where multiple SQLite database files (`paelladoc_memory.db`) were being created in different locations due to inconsistent path handling.

**Changes:**

*   Unified the default database path in `SQLiteMemoryAdapter` to reliably point to the project root (`PROJECT_ROOT / "paelladoc_memory.db"`).
*   Removed explicit/incorrect path overrides in core plugins (`paella`, `list_projects`, `continue`) to use the adapter's default path.
*   Fixed a minor pre-commit hook error (unused variable) in `continue_proj.py`.

This ensures all parts of the application consistently use the single database file located at the project root, improving portability and resolving the scattered database file issue.

author: akuzni2
body:
Adds an adapter to convert between AddressBook and Datastore.

Some components still use AddressBook instead of the newer DataStore. When domain-specific changes depend on shared/common components, it's helpful to temporarily allow domain components to switch back from DataStore to AddressBook. This enables backward compatibility so that components using either AddressBook or DataStore can function while waiting for the common codebase to fully upgrade from AddressBook to DataStore.

This pull request introduces new functionality for handling branch clinic application requests in the `BEAUTIFY_QUERY` system. The changes include adding query handlers, extending data models, and updating API endpoints to support fetching and managing branch clinic application data.

### New Query Handlers for Branch Clinic Applications:
* Added `GetAllApplyBranchRequestQueryHandler` to fetch paginated lists of branch clinic application requests. This includes filtering by clinic ID and application status. (`BEAUTIFY_QUERY.APPLICATION/UseCases/Queries/Clinics/GetAllApplyBranchRequestQueryHandler.cs`, [BEAUTIFY_QUERY.APPLICATION/UseCases/Queries/Clinics/GetAllApplyBranchRequestQueryHandler.csR1-R54](diffhunk://#diff-66b4bfb50457536a49a01519240b9d38d02894eebe1e08a5139d3748d4cfd54eR1-R54))
* Added `GetDetailBranchApplyRequestQueryHandler` to fetch detailed information about a specific branch clinic application request. (`BEAUTIFY_QUERY.APPLICATION/UseCases/Queries/Clinics/GetDetailBranchApplyRequestQueryHandler.cs`, [BEAUTIFY_QUERY.APPLICATION/UseCases/Queries/Clinics/GetDetailBranchApplyRequestQueryHandler.csR1-R64](diffhunk://#diff-83b21cdace57c94d62de5338de44f3eebc262ad506687e197005f825063628c4R1-R64))

### Updates to Data Models:
* Introduced `BranchClinicApplyGetAll` and `BranchClinicApplyDetail` response models to structure data for branch clinic application requests. (`BEAUTIFY_QUERY.CONTRACT/Services/Clinics/Response.cs`, [BEAUTIFY_QUERY.CONTRACT/Services/Clinics/Response.csR121-R172](diffhunk://#diff-65b6c38677c186a2d232ac1ad0f3312ef063d9543912341d787c7c7bb09a2ea5R121-R172))
* Added `IsMain` property to the `ClinicOnBoardingRequest` entity to distinguish between main and branch clinics. (`BEAUTIFY_QUERY.DOMAIN/Entities/ClinicOnBoardingRequest.cs`, [BEAUTIFY_QUERY.DOMAIN/Entities/ClinicOnBoardingRequest.csR11](diffhunk://#diff-ce07104f47f96d8149679164b3e8d545cee7a491b06b33dacba8c6ade4d7b828R11))

### API Enhancements:
* Added new endpoints to fetch all branch clinic applications (`GetAllApplyClinicRequest`) and detailed branch clinic application data (`GetDetailBranchApplyRequest`). These endpoints require authorization. (`BEAUTIFY_QUERY.PRESENTATION/APIs/Clinics/ClinicApi.cs`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5cb58012eb60ef1ce2eebe745854f230ea3453cefbcaca60d861c1dbaf9d7414R15-R44) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5cb58012eb60ef1ce2eebe745854f230ea3453cefbcaca60d861c1dbaf9d7414R110-R128)

author: iamevanyt
body:
<!-- Please include a description of changes. -->

## Changes

- Added `extensions.handleCrxRequest()`
- Added option `registerCrxProtocolInDefaultSession` when creating an `ElectronChromeExtensions` instance
- Update README to include initialization warning

---

## Problem

When having multiple sessions with multiple instances of `ElectronChromeExtensions`, using `crx` in the default session will only result in one of the session's extension icons being able to load.

## Solutions

- Expose `extensions.handleCrxRequest()` to allow custom handling
- Add an option to prevent handling it automatically in default session.

## Sample Code

```ts
// Register CRX protocol in default session
app.whenReady().then(() => {
  protocol.handle("crx", async (request) => {
    const url = URL.parse(request.url);
    if (!url) {
      return new Response("Invalid URL", { status: 404 });
    }

    const partition = url?.searchParams.get("partition");
    if (!partition) {
      return new Response("No partition", { status: 400 });
    }

    const partitionSession = session.fromPartition(partition);

    const extensions = ElectronChromeExtensions.fromSession(partitionSession);
    if (!extensions) {
      return new Response("Extensions not found", { status: 404 });
    }

    return extensions.handleCrxRequest(request);
  });
});
```

author: jmccardle
body:
This is my attempt to put the Gotchi behavior into a class. My primary goal was feature parity and low-level access to how the terminal app already worked, and should result in zero observable behavior differences when running the program interactively.

How to use it:

```python
from main import Gotchi
pet = Gotchi()

pet.feed(); pet.play(); pet.sleep() # the commands available at the terminal

pet.draw() # print the lines the terminal app would display

pet.generate_display_lines() # get a list of strings, that would be displayed in terminal

pet.step() # by default does a single step

pet.step(100000) # will return after about 7200 steps because the pet died
```

It's "an exercise for the reader" to connect the Gotchi class to a website, an LLM, model context protocol server, etc.

author: dhiren-mhatre
body:
## Change Description
Fix issue #9708 by checking for existing SQLite database files before warning about bbolt files.

Currently, when users start LND with the SQLite backend, they see warnings about existing bbolt database files even if they've already migrated their data using `lndinit migrate-db`. This PR enhances the warning system to only display these messages when a SQLite file doesn't exist yet, reducing confusion for users who have already completed migration.

## Steps to Test
1. Create a test environment with bbolt database files:
   ```
   mkdir -p ~/lnd-test-bolt
   lnd --lnddir=~/lnd-test-bolt --datadir=~/lnd-test-bolt
   # Create and fund a wallet
   lncli --lnddir=~/lnd-test-bolt create
   ```

2. Migrate to SQLite:
   ```
   lndinit --lnddir=~/lnd-test-bolt migrate-db
   ```

3. Run with SQLite backend before applying this fix:
   ```
   lnd --lnddir=~/lnd-test-bolt --db.backend=sqlite --db.use-native-sql
   ```
   Observe the warnings about existing bbolt files.

4. Run with SQLite backend after applying this fix:
   ```
   lnd --lnddir=~/lnd-test-bolt --db.backend=sqlite --db.use-native-sql
   ```
   No warnings should appear since SQLite files exist.

5. Delete the SQLite files and run again:
   ```
   rm ~/lnd-test-bolt/data/chain/bitcoin/regtest/chain.sqlite
   rm ~/lnd-test-bolt/data/graph/regtest/channel.sqlite
   lnd --lnddir=~/lnd-test-bolt --db.backend=sqlite --db.use-native-sql
   ```
   Warnings should reappear because bbolt files exist but SQLite files don't.

## Pull Request Checklist
### Testing
- [x] Your PR passes all CI checks.
- [x] Tests covering the positive and negative (error paths) are included.
- [x] Bug fixes contain tests triggering the bug to prevent regressions.
### Code Style and Documentation
- [x] The change is not [insubstantial](https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/blob/master/docs/code_contribution_guidelines.md#substantial-contributions-only).
- [x] The change obeys the [Code Documentation and Commenting](https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/blob/master/docs/development_guidelines.md#code-documentation-and-commenting) guidelines, and lines wrap at 80.
- [x] Commits follow the [Ideal Git Commit Structure](https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/blob/master/docs/development_guidelines.md#ideal-git-commit-structure).
- [x] Any new logging statements use an appropriate subsystem and logging level.
- [x] Any new lncli commands have appropriate tags in the comments for the rpc in the proto file.
- [x] [There is a change description in the release notes](https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/tree/master/docs/release-notes).

author: dcollins15
body:
As a follow-up to #9828, this PR further refines `merge.SCTAssay` with better documentation, more informative warnings, and some tests. The bug in question is encountered when running merge on `SCTAssay`s containing multiple models. An `SCTAssay` will contain multiple models if:

a. It has already been merged with another `SCTAssay`.
b. `SCTransform` was called on a multi-layer assay.

The following script can be used to verify that it has been resolved:

```
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratData)


ifnb <- LoadData("ifnb")
ifnb[["RNA"]] <- split(ifnb[["RNA"]], f = ifnb$stim)
ifnb <- SCTransform(ifnb)

pbmc <- LoadData("pbmc3k")
pbmc <- SCTransform(pbmc)


merge(ifnb, pbmc)
```

author: cryo81
body:
Implementing C++17 best practices toward unused variable.
Details :
The class NamedObjectFactory needs the "playerbot* ai" parameter, which is used in the inherited class NamedObjectContext, in charge of managing the objects (creation, update and reset).

Various function (named after character spells) are assigned to the ActionCreator map. This map requiring the parameter to work, it can't be quitted from these functions, despite the fact they (the functions) are not using this parameter (playerbot*) themselves.

Good practice in this case is to replace :
`PlayerbotAI* botAI`
by
`[[maybe_unused]] PlayerbotAI* botAI`

Warning solved in debian (using clang++ 14.0.6) : 272 / 1135

body:
scenario: you have a global .gitattributes for settings crlf, text/binary, diff etc settings

then this is what you get

```
$ transcrypt --list-contexts                                                                                                                                                             default (no patterns in .gitattributes)
custom (no patterns in .gitattributes)
```

instead of

```
$ transcrypt --list-contexts                                                                                                                                                             default
custom
```

although the .gitattributes in the repo has the patterns defined

Point is: do we really support transcrypt globally? with custom contexts?
If we do, then we need to check all attributes files, not only the first one.

PS: on a different note, it also doesn't make sense (to me at least) that `--add=<pattern>` write to anything but a local gitattributes

author: evelynzapata20
body:
This pull request introduces a feature for sending messages to TikTok influencers, along with several related improvements to the codebase. The key changes include adding a new API endpoint for sending messages, implementing the message-sending functionality using Selenium, and enhancing the WebDriver utility to support proper cleanup. Additionally, CORS middleware has been added to the application for improved compatibility with frontend clients.

### New Feature: Sending Messages to TikTok Influencers
* Added a new POST endpoint `/api/v1/messages/{username}` in `app/routes/routes.py` to send messages to TikTok influencers. This endpoint validates the input, calls the message-sending use case, and handles errors appropriately.
* Implemented the `send_message_to_influencer` use case in `app/use_cases/send_message_to_influencer.py`, which constructs the TikTok profile URL and delegates the message-sending logic to the service layer.

### Message-Sending Implementation
* Created `send_message` in `app/services/messages/send_messages.py`, which uses Selenium to automate sending messages to TikTok profiles. It includes message cleaning, error handling, and proper delays to mimic human interaction.

### WebDriver Enhancements
* Added a `close_driver` method in `app/utils/web_driver.py` to ensure the WebDriver instance is properly closed and cleaned up after use. This prevents resource leaks and improves reliability.

### Middleware and API Improvements
* Integrated CORS middleware in `main.py` to allow cross-origin requests, enabling seamless integration with frontend applications.

# CI Pipeline Setup for amMentor Backend

## What I did

This PR sets up the GitHub Actions-based CI pipeline for the Django backend. It’s meant to run basic checks like migrations, collectstatic, and tests on every push and PR to main.

CI is now part of the workflow — no more “it works on my machine” 


## What’s included
- ✅ Added .github/workflows/ci.yml
- ✅ Spins up a Postgres container via services
- ✅ Runs makemigrations, migrate, collectstatic, and Django tests
- ✅ Uses Python 3.11 for compatibility with the project


## About the secrets
- I’ve set it up to expect secrets from GitHub Actions (like SQL_NAME, SQL_USER, etc.)
- BUT: added fallback dummy values using the || operator, so the pipeline won’t fail if the maintainer hasn’t added secrets yet.

## What’s next?
- Just need to merge and check that the pipeline triggers properly
- Once confirmed, we can improve it later with coverage reports, linting, deployment steps, etc.

body:
Just wanted to share my implementation of a simple find/replace dialog for the multi-tack Track Info dialog.
It's mainly supposed to help with how I use comments usage/workflow:
first line of the track comment is always a row of tags, like genre, and some other hints, which I can easily edit in the decks (only first line is shown in that editor).
Now I can mass-replace tags, eg. classic -> klassik, tekno -> techno

**Select** uses the current implementation with the combobox and text editor.
**Find/replace** switches to the Find & Replace mask and replaces the first occurence of the text
Just one special feature ( which could actually be the 3rd mode "Insert"):
if the **Find** field is empty, the replace string (+ whitespace) is inserted before the comment.

I'll probably tweak standard find/replace to parse only the first line of the comment to not accidentally mess up my Bandcamp album/track links in line 3.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d8cbd9d-bd08-46df-9dd1-810c37167c4c)

If there is interest I'll make it ready to be merged.
